Concretely, we define deterministic probe-dependent ``template residuals,'' fit low-dimensional correction coefficients, and then evaluate held-out discrepancies (chi-square/RMSE) under the public covariance. This approach establishes the audit protocol, probe splitting, masking, and reproducible bookkeeping under realistic vector/covariance dimensions, but it does not constitute a physical reproduction of the DES Y3 3`×`2pt likelihood . The repository includes a plug-in backend interface and an environment probe; in the baseline environment, the physical backend import fails (e.g., pyccl unavailable), motivating this staged presentation.

name: Carrier, actions, lens
compact: A carrier is a finite set `X` of states. A transition/action family over `X` is a finite set `A` of actions with, for each `a∈ A`, either a map `F_a : X → X` or a row-stochastic kernel `P_a` on `X`; whether dynamics are deterministic or stochastic is declared per construction. A lens (observation map) is a map `q : X → Y` onto a finite value set; its fibers form the observational partition ` _q` of `X`. A policy for `q` is a feedback rule that selects actions measurably with respect to ` _q` (more generally, with respect to the history of `q`-values).

name: Predictive and observational equivalence
compact: Fix a carrier with declared dynamics and a lens `q`. Two states (or histories) are observationally equivalent when all admissible current observables agree on them; the induced quotient is the current public quotient `Q`. They are predictively equivalent when they agree on the full family of admissible future behavior (continuation laws, or distributions over future observable trajectories under all admissible continuations); the induced quotient is the predictive quotient `M`. Predictive equivalence refines observational equivalence, giving a canonical comparison map ` : M → Q`. The gap between them, same `Q`-class with different `M`-class, is a factorization defect and is the recurring engine of this paper.

When a closure-like operator `E` is only approximately idempotent, its idempotence defect ` (E)= 12 _z E^2(z, )-E(z, ) _1` is computed exactly and reported rather than assumed small. An audit is a declared, executable check on a construction, such as a defect computation, a control run, or an exhaustive comparison, whose outcome is recorded with the result. A gate is a named audit whose passage is required before a claim may be graded; the gate vocabulary used here (sufficiency, descent, stability, control-of-content, no-smuggling, visibility, audit, strictness) is imported from the interaction calculus of the companion corpus (Appendix app:imports) and is used as a reporting format, not re-proved.

label: def:cpackage
compact: def:cpackage The full C-package ` ` is the eight-clause full-design and audit contract `C1`--`C8`, together with cross-clause coherence data and a full promotion-gate panel. A candidate consists of a carrier `X`, declared transition/action families, a public lens and exposure channels, a predictive self-lens, branch structure, a maintenance ledger, and protocol generators; the clauses constrain that data as follows. • A declared multiscale exposure-closure family with robust fixed-point structure: closure operators `E_ ` at declared stagings ` `, exact fixed-point and defect bookkeeping, and perturbation audits with declared retention thresholds. • A strict promoted distinction across declared layers: ` ( _0, _1)≠∅` for the declared lower and promoted readouts, certified by a split pair. • A recursively stable self-coordinate: refinement of the public self-lens by dynamical profiles terminates at a predictive quotient that carries the package's own continuation coordinate. • The determining predictive state is not exposed relative to the declared public channel family: no admissible current observable factors through it non-constantly on the realized support. Hiddenness is channel-relative by construction. • A declared audit of action credit: generator provenance routes computed directionality into self, other, or none, with scheduled and internalized controls that must not be credited as self. • A maintained, funded order/tick/arrow structure: a staged phase carrier that persists and progresses under budget, with the arrow carried by the package's own audit channel rather than by external scheduling. • Strict recombination refinement over the branchwise quotient: joint content over declared branches, witnessed by ` ` (Section sec:structure). • Nonempty maintained viability: ` ≠∅` under the declared maintenance ledger, with underfunding collapsing the kernel.

paper_title: An Audited Closure Architecture for Consciousness: — Exact Finite Models, Structural Theorems, and Conditional Realization
name: T1-L1, the self-wheel
label: con:t1
compact: con:t1 The carrier is `Z = P × W` with `|P|=6` public positions and `|W|=2` hidden phases, so `N = |Z| = 12`. The public self-lens is `q(p,w)=p`: the system can observe its own position but not its phase. The dynamics contain a live, unobserved phase slip with exact branch weights `3/4` and `1/4`, placed so that public history does not reconstruct the phase: the public trace `(1,2,1)` can end in either phase. A deadline makes the hidden phase viability-relevant: continuation beyond the deadline requires acting on the phase-dependent continuation law, and a wrong commitment exits the safe set.

name: Exact forcing and minimal restoration; T1
label: thm:t1
compact: thm:t1 Grade: theorem-grade on the exact T1-L1 carrier; conditional family schema beyond it. Scope: the declared twelve-state deadline carrier, its action family, and its lens. On this carrier: • Public exhaustion. Every `q`-measurable feedback policy has an empty deadline viability kernel: ` (q) = ∅`, by exhaustive enumeration of all public-lens policies. • Predictive restoration. The five-class continuation-law abstraction `L` restores a ten-state kernel, and the canonical predictive quotient `M = q × L` restores exactly the same ten states: ` (L) = (M)`, `| (M)| = 10`, certified by a separate nine-class search and a refinement audit. • Unique minimal repair. Among all `64` refinements of the public lens, the unique minimal closure-restoring refinement is the seven-class quotient ` _*` that splits exactly the public fiber `p=1`; every closure-restoring refinement splits that fiber, and the maximal refinement that leaves `p=1` unsplit has empty kernel. Assumptions: deadline active; live, resettable, non-publicly-definable phase. Nonclaim: this does not show that all bounded self-predicting systems must form selves, and it is not an empirical result about any actual system.

paper_title: An Audited Closure Architecture for Consciousness: — Exact Finite Models, Structural Theorems, and Conditional Realization
name: Interface-relative non-exposure; T2
compact: Grade: theorem-grade direct finite instantiation; the C4 condition is generic and declared, not universal. Scope: the declared channel family ` ` on the finite privacy-wheel carrier. Under non-exposure with predictive witness content, there is a connector loop that fixes every current public class while moving the predictive class. On the exact carrier: two hidden states, one public class; the loop moves `0/1` of `Q`-classes and `1/1` of `M`-classes. Adding a public `M`-reading channel dissolves the witness (the dissolution control); the degenerate `M=Q` control has no witness and licenses no privacy claim. Nonclaim: nothing is private under every possible interface, and hiddenness does not imply phenomenality.

paper_title: An Audited Closure Architecture for Consciousness: — Exact Finite Models, Structural Theorems, and Conditional Realization
name: No-shortcut corollary; T3
compact: Grade: corollary-grade. Scope: declared source and target maps on a fixed finite interface. If the promoted content is strict over the public layer, no lower-layer shortcut derivation recovers it: the factor map does not exist, and any closed lower-layer compression fails closure for the promoted readout. Contrapositive: if a proposed derivation succeeds, the extension was never strict. On the exact carrier (reusing the T9 support below), the strict case computes factor attempt `=` none from the shared-report pair; the control with report as both source and target computes a concrete factor map and no gap. Nonclaim: this neither solves nor dissolves the philosophical explanatory gap in general, asserts no hidden substance, and does not say mechanism is absent: if a derivation succeeds, the content was non-strict, not unmechanistic.

paper_title: An Audited Closure Architecture for Consciousness: — Exact Finite Models, Structural Theorems, and Conditional Realization
name: Report descent and no-overreading; T9
compact: Grade: direct instantiation of imported audit theorems plus finite toy witness. Scope: declared report and no-report interfaces on a three-state hidden support. A valid report licenses only its descended boundary object, never the hidden structure. The finite content: the report map is non-injective (states `u_0 ≠ u_1` share the report boundary `r_shared`), while a differently scoped no-report instrument distinguishes the same pair; an overreaching claim (suppressed unbridged use) classifies as blocked, and a visible descent-only claim classifies as accepted, under the same vendored classifier. Nonclaim: reports are not useless or disconnected; and hidden content is not inaccessible to all possible instruments, since the no-report instrument in the same study distinguishes what the report identifies.

The positive residue of clauses 2--3 is bounded-observer ignorance under declared packaging and budget, not substrate spontaneity. • Deflation foreclosed -flavored. ``Only a lower-layer event'' commits the factorization error: once the layer is strict, the layer claim cannot be replaced by a base-layer paraphrase without losing the certificate, as T3 establishes. paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Residual partial order
label: def:aor:residual-partial-order
compact: def:aor:residual-partial-order The relation ` _res` on ` ` is generated by: (i) atom refinement, `a _resb` when `a` is obtained from `b` by splitting along a finer probe family or stage; (ii) type inclusion, `a _resb` when `a` has `b`'s primary type together with strictly more forced secondary types than `b`; and (iii) componentwise products. It is a partial order on isomorphism classes of residual records.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Residual atom
label: def:aor:residual-atom
compact: def:aor:residual-atom A residual record `a∈ ` is an atom if it is minimal under ` _res` among non-empty records. Equivalently, `a` has a unique primary type and no proper non-empty refinement.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Atom decomposition
label: thm:aor:atom-decomposition
compact: thm:aor:atom-decomposition Every residual record `r∈ ` admits a finite decomposition `r= _i a_i` as a disjoint sum of atoms. The decomposition is unique up to permutation, and is computable from the carrier field data.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Residual product
label: thm:aor:residual-product
compact: thm:aor:residual-product The product of two PreSB carriers ` C_1` and ` C_2` over the same scope (componentwise product of all seventeen fields) has residual stratum ` ( C_1× C_2) = ( C_1) ( C_2) ^cross( C_1, C_2)`, where ` ^cross` collects only those residuals whose primary type is ` `, ` `, ` `, or ` ` and that arise from the product pairing. In particular the eight other primary types are additive across products.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Forced-residual theorem
label: thm:aor:forced-residual
compact: thm:aor:forced-residual For each primary residual type ` _*`, there is a fixed minimal set of forced secondary types that any non-empty record of primary type ` _*` must also exhibit. The complete forced-secondary list is recorded in tab:aor-forced-secondary-types. Forcing is faithful: any discharge that closes the primary type without simultaneously closing each forced secondary type leaves a non-empty ` ` entry.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: AOR-8 status catalogue
label: def:aor:aor-8-statuses
compact: def:aor:aor-8-statuses The AOR-8 status catalogue is the eleven-entry vocabulary of discharge statuses for ` ` records: zero, budgeted, bridged, hidden, moduli, selected, probabilistic, out\_of\_scope, nonclaim, blocked, approved\_other. The asymptotic extensions (def:aor:asymptotic-statuses) add asymptotic\_budgeted, summable, contractive, eventual\_zero for limit-stage records.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Discharge record
label: def:aor:discharge-record
compact: def:aor:discharge-record A discharge record on a residual atom `a∈ ` is a triple `(a,s, )` with `s` an AOR-8 status (or asymptotic extension) and ` ` a typed witness payload appropriate to `s`: a positivity proof for zero; a finite budget bound for budgeted; a bridging carrier identifier for bridged; a moduli space pin for moduli; a selection rule for selected; a measure record for probabilistic; a scope reference for out\_of\_scope and nonclaim; a block reason for blocked; an external-record citation for approved\_other; or an asymptotic-witness payload as appropriate.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Discharge witness
label: def:aor:discharge-witness
compact: def:aor:discharge-witness A discharge witness for a residual record `r= _i a_i` is a family `(a_i,s_i, _i)` of discharge records, one per atom in the decomposition of `r`. The witness closes `r` if every status `s_i` is a declared base AOR-8 status, or an asymptotic extension for a limit-stage residual atom, and every forced-secondary type of `a_i` also has a discharge record in the witness.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Cost record
label: def:aor:cost-record
compact: def:aor:cost-record For each pair `(t,s)` with `t` a residual type and `s` a status, the cost record `Cost(t,s)` is a finite multiset of `(t',s')` pairs called the downstream obligations generated by paying a `t`-atom with status `s`. Cost records are tabulated in the `143`-entry base cost table `Cost:Types× Statuses→ P_fin(Types× Statuses)`.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Downstream operator
label: def:aor:down-operator
compact: def:aor:down-operator The downstream operator `Down` acts on a residual record `r` with discharge witness `(a_i,s_i, _i)` by \[ Down(r,\(a_i,s_i, _i)\) = _i Cost(type(a_i),s_i) \] viewed as a new residual record of fresh atoms to be statused.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Cost table
label: def:aor:cost-table
compact: def:aor:cost-table The cost table is the function `Cost:Types×Statuses→ P_fin(Types×Statuses)` with `13` residual types and `11` base AOR-8 statuses, totalling `143` entries. Cost-free pairs `(t,s)` are exactly those with `Cost(t,s)=∅`.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Cost-table admissibility
label: lem:aor:cost-table-admissibility
compact: lem:aor:cost-table-admissibility The base cost table of def:aor:cost-table, together with the asymptotic companion rows used for refinement-chain discharge, satisfies two admissibility properties: • Strict descent. For every cost-table or asymptotic companion row \(Down(a,s)=w\), the output multiset \(w\) is strictly less than the singleton multiset \(\(a,s)\\) in the Dershowitz--Manna multiset extension of the well-founded order on the status coordinate, where base statuses are ordered by the rank of def:aor:aor-8-statuses, zero is the unique minimum and contractive, eventual\_zero, summable, and asymptotic\_budgeted ordered above zero but below the base non-terminal statuses budgeted, bridged, hidden, moduli, selected, probabilistic, out\_of\_scope, nonclaim, blocked, approved\_other, with summable<asymptotic\_budgeted inside the asymptotic tier. Concretely, every output element \((t',s')∈ w\) satisfies \(s'<s\) in this status order; the primary type coordinate is unconstrained. • Local diamond. For every record \(r\) with two distinct cost-table moves \(r→ r_1\) and \(r→ r_2\), there exists a common cost-table-reachable record \(r_*\) with \(r_1→^* r_*\) and \(r_2→^* r_*\).

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Cascade graph
label: def:aor:cascade-graph
compact: def:aor:cascade-graph The cascade graph of a residual record `r` is the bipartite labelled multigraph `G(r)` whose vertices are residual-record atoms and discharge witnesses (alternating layers), and whose edges record the downstream obligations produced by `Down`. Edges are weighted by their AOR-8 status.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Bipartite cascade graph
label: thm:aor:cascade-bipartite
compact: thm:aor:cascade-bipartite For every residual record `r` and every choice of discharge witness, the cascade graph `G(r)` is bipartite: edges alternate between atom-vertices and witness-vertices, and no edge connects two vertices of the same kind.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Cascade termination
label: thm:aor:cascade-termination
compact: thm:aor:cascade-termination The cascade graph `G(r)` is well-founded under the status-multiset measure induced by the AOR-8 status rank and the Dershowitz--Manna multiset extension. In particular every cascade terminates in finitely many discharge steps.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Cascade confluence
label: thm:aor:cascade-confluence
compact: thm:aor:cascade-confluence The discharge relation on ` ` is locally confluent: if a residual atom admits two distinct one-step discharges into records `r_1` and `r_2`, then there exists a record `r_3` reached by further discharges from both `r_1` and `r_2`. Together with termination (thm:aor:cascade-termination), Newman's lemma yields global confluence : every cascade has a unique normal form.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Cross-cascade composition
label: thm:aor:cross-cascade-composition
compact: thm:aor:cross-cascade-composition For two residual records `r_1` and `r_2` on the same carrier, their disjoint-union cascade `G(r_1 r_2)` equals the disjoint union of cascades `G(r_1) G(r_2)` together with the cross-edges generated by interaction atoms of primary type ` `, ` `, ` `, or ` ` produced by the residual-product theorem (thm:aor:residual-product).

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Cascade-stable AOR
label: def:aor:cascade-stable-aor
compact: def:aor:cascade-stable-aor A PreSB carrier ` C∈ _ S` is cascade-stable if every residual record in ` ( C)` admits a discharge witness whose cascade reaches the empty record in finitely many steps using only the base AOR-8 statuses (def:aor:aor-8-statuses). The class of cascade-stable AOR carriers is denoted ` _ S`.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Cascade-stable characterisation
label: thm:aor:cascade-stable-characterisation
compact: thm:aor:cascade-stable-characterisation ` C∈ _ S` if and only if every ` `-atom of ` C` has a declared discharge status whose cost-table walk reaches a cost-free terminal status in finitely many moves. Equivalently, the ` `-iteration of `Down` from the initial atoms of ` C` produces an eventually empty sequence of records.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Refinement morphism
label: def:aor:refinement-morphism
compact: def:aor:refinement-morphism A refinement morphism ` : C→ C'` between two PreSB carriers is a PreSB morphism that additionally records, for each field, whether it is an A1--A6 refinement step (def:aor:refinement-kinds-six). Refinement morphisms compose and have identities. The category ` _ S` has PreSB carriers as objects and refinement morphisms as arrows.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Six refinement kinds
label: def:aor:refinement-kinds-six
compact: def:aor:refinement-kinds-six A refinement morphism's per-field annotations belong to one of six disjoint kinds: A1 scope expansion (enlarging ` S` within a fixed scope chain); A2 record-field expansion (adding admissible records to one of the registries); A3 stage / refinement-axis growth (extending `Stage` by a new stage); A4 constraint tightening (replacing a constraint by a strictly stronger one); A5 morphism strengthening (replacing a morphism by a refinement of itself); A6 carrier (probe / target) refinement (replacing `(H,q,Q)` or a probe/target family by a finer version, with a declared projection map).

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: ` ` category
label: def:aor:refpresb-category
compact: def:aor:refpresb-category The category ` _ S` is the full category of PreSB carriers of scope ` S` with refinement morphisms. A refinement chain is a directed diagram in ` _ S` indexed by a directed poset.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: ` ` is directed-cocomplete
label: thm:aor:refpresb-cocomplete
compact: thm:aor:refpresb-cocomplete The category ` _ S` has all directed colimits. Concretely, for a directed diagram `( C_j, _jj')` with projections `p_jj': C_j'→ C_j` along reverse arrows, the colimit object ` C_∈fty=colim_j C_j` has record/scope data as the directed union of the corresponding ` C_j` data, and carrier data as the inverse limit of compatible threads under the projections `p_jj'`. The construction is functorial and preserves PreSB-typing.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Asymptotic statuses
label: def:aor:asymptotic-statuses
compact: def:aor:asymptotic-statuses For a residual atom `a` of a colimit object ` C_∈fty=colim_j C_j`, the asymptotic statuses extending AOR-8 are: asymptotic\_budgeted (there exists a uniform finite budget `B` and a tail index `J_0` with the per-stage cost bounded by `B` for all `j J_0`); summable (the per-stage costs are summable across the directed chain); contractive (the per-stage cost ratios tend to a constant strictly less than `1`); eventual\_zero (the per-stage cost is zero for all `j J_0` for some tail index `J_0`).

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Asymptotic soundness
label: thm:aor:asymptotic-soundness
compact: thm:aor:asymptotic-soundness The four asymptotic statuses of def:aor:asymptotic-statuses satisfy the implication chain \[ eventual\_zero contractive summable asymptotic\_budgeted. \] Each asymptotic status closes the colimit residual at level ` ` without producing a fresh atom in the limit. Moreover, if every atom of ` C_∈fty` has an asymptotic status from this list and every finite stage ` C_j` is in ` _ S`, then ` C_∈fty∈ _ S`.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Refinement-stable AOR
label: def:aor:refinement-stable-aor
compact: def:aor:refinement-stable-aor A PreSB carrier ` C∈ _ S` is refinement-stable if AOR-membership is preserved by every refinement morphism into ` C` and by every directed colimit of refinement chains terminating at ` C`. The class of refinement-stable AOR carriers is denoted ` _ S`.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Refinement-stable characterisation
label: thm:aor:refinement-stable-characterisation
compact: thm:aor:refinement-stable-characterisation ` C∈ _ S` if and only if (i) ` C∈ _ S` and (ii) every residual atom of ` C` that survives a colimit step is paid by an asymptotic status from def:aor:asymptotic-statuses. Equivalently, every refinement chain terminating at ` C` has a discharge witness in which limit-stage atoms carry asymptotic statuses.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: Hierarchy witnesses
label: thm:aor:hierarchy
compact: thm:aor:hierarchy There exist two named carriers \( C_witness,1\) and \( C_witness,2\), together with typed obstruction markers, that witness the failure of the stronger stability conditions: \( C_witness,1\) lies in \( _ S\) and carries a typed obstruction marker certifying that it does not satisfy the refinement-stability predicate; \( C_witness,2\) lies in \( _ S\) and carries a typed obstruction marker certifying that it does not satisfy the cascade-stability predicate.

paper_title: Audited Operational Realisability: — A Closure-Completion Reflection for Carriers with Audit Data
name: No strong-realism reading of AOR
label: nonclaim:aor:no-strong-realism
compact: nonclaim:aor:no-strong-realism Membership in ` _ S` is not a metaphysical or philosophical realism claim about the carrier's underlying domain. It is a record-level audit predicate: every declared record is typed, every cited route is audited, every residual is statused, and every nonclaim is registered, within the declared scope ` S`. Any extra-scope interpretation requires its own audit and is outside the present framework.

paper_title: Carrier Exactification after Promotion on Fixed Support in Six Birds Theory

paper_title: Carrier Exactification after Promotion on Fixed Support in Six Birds Theory
name: Criterion implication, abstract form
label: prop:criterion-implication

Then `C` satisfies the paper's seven criteria on ` `: C1 via `RS(C, S_des)`; C2 via `TC(C)` together with `RTC(C)`; C3 via `C D_i` for every `i`; C4 via `SH(C)`; C5 via `PH(C)`; C6 via `EH(C)`; and C7 via `CS(C, S_des)`. paper_title: Carrier Exactification after Promotion on Fixed Support in Six Birds Theory

paper_title: Hiddenness as a Structural Law of Emergence
name: Computational substrate
label: def:substrate
compact: def:substrate A computational substrate \( \) is a typed bounded polynomial-time computation context . It consists of: • an instance family \(X_ \); • a size function on instances together with a bound \(N_ \), so that only instances of size at most \(N_ \) belong to the bounded carrier considered here; • a declared solver-prefix family, assigning to each bounded instance the finite trace shape that a polynomial-time computation may generate before the history is audited. A substrate is therefore the typed context in which instances, scale, and trace formation have all been fixed, rather than a language or a set of inputs.

paper_title: Hiddenness as a Structural Law of Emergence
name: Example: 3-SAT substrate
compact: Fix a bound \(N\). One may take \(X_ \) to be the family of 3-CNF formulas of size at most \(N\), measured for instance by the number of variables and clauses . The solver-prefix family can be a declared polynomial-time decision-attempt policy: for each formula it records the finite sequence of inspected clauses, partial assignments, branching choices, local simplifications, and time-certificate data produced before the bounded audit closes. No completeness claim for 3-SAT is built into this example; the substrate only declares the finite typed traces on which the later quotients will act.

name: Strength stratification
compact: The later statement refers to a four-level strength stratification \[ 1,\ 2,\ 3,\ 4 \] for coupling functions used inside \(gen_ \). paper_title: Hiddenness as a Structural Law of Emergence
name: \( \) is not a bijection onto \(P\)
label: prop:c1-not-bijective
compact: prop:c1-not-bijective The projection \( \) is not a bijection from \( \) onto the standard class \(P\). The obstruction has three parts. • Histories versus languages. A \( \)-class is a class of histories, possibly over a single bounded instance. A polynomial-time decision predicate is a function on all inputs. A single current class does not by itself define a language predicate over all input strings. • Trace observables beyond decision output. The quotient \( \) identifies histories by equality of all declared polynomial-time current observables, not merely by equality of the decision bit. Two histories computing the same language may still be \( \)-distinct because their trace, solver-prefix, or audit bookkeeping observables differ. • Machine multiplicity. Different polynomial-time machines may decide the same language while producing different \( \)-observable histories on the same instance. These histories can map to different current classes but to the same language predicate.

paper_title: Hiddenness as a Structural Law of Emergence

compact: The is a framework-internal structural law at diagnosis grade over predictive-quotient holonomy on autonomous-lifted polynomial-time substrates; it does not imply standard \(P≠ NP\). paper_title: Hiddenness as a Structural Law of Emergence
name: Nonclaim: no asymptotic theorem-grade CSL
compact: The is hardened to diagnosis grade by the cascade work it summarizes: bounded finite-carrier evidence with falsifier audit. It is not stated as an asymptotic theorem over all polynomial-time computation histories. The empirical hardening is a paper-side certification rather than a derivable consequence of the lemma's formal content; the boundary is set explicitly by the qualifier.

paper_title: Hiddenness as a Structural Law of Emergence
name: Nonclaim: no representation theorem
compact: The granularity-mismatch theorem at R-Diagnosis identifies the structural obstruction; the representation theorem is named but not constructed. More explicitly, the theorem identifies the structural obstruction between the framework's typed quotients and the standard \(P\)/\(NP\) language classes, and it exhibits a constructive finite-carrier witness for the existential conclusion. The bridging representation theorem from arbitrary polynomial-time deciders to autonomous-lift carriers preserving witness-content exposure is the asymptotic step this paper does not establish; the grade label records this gap explicitly.

paper_title: Hiddenness as a Structural Law of Emergence
name: Additional nonclaims
compact: The framework is similar in spirit to, but structurally distinct from, the natural-proofs barrier of Razborov--Rudich , the algebrization barrier of Aaronson--Wigderson , and the relativization barrier of Baker--Gill--Solovay . The predictive-quotient holonomy carrier is not a circumvention of any of those three barriers in their native senses; the relationship is discussed in sec:discussion. The framework also uses standard mathematical constructions throughout: quotients of finite carriers, projection maps, the equivalence of refinement and surjection between quotient relations, and finite Boolean carriers for the granularity-mismatch witness. The contribution is the typed apparatus and the granularity-mismatch packaging, not these underlying mathematical constructions.

paper_title: Institutions Are Strict Extensions of the Game

The new common-history distinctions occur in the formation window and not at the already saturated rounds.

By contrast, one-sided probe loops can leave equal current observations and different predictive states, because the free responses observed during the probe refine the posterior over rule pairs.

Every surviving noisy witness is currentizable under the declared richer current descriptions, and no coherent-memory class is awarded on the tested grid and window.

compact: def:descended-interfaces Let `P` be a candidate promoted package on a fixed comparison surface ` C`. We say that `P` has signature-level descended update support on ` C` if the retained lower-generator interface descends to a coherent promoted-level action or closure interface on ` C`. paper_title: Internal Structure of a Surviving Promoted Package on Fixed Support in Six Birds Theory

label: def:stability-honesty

We say that `P` is protocol honest if its apparent support does not depend on pre-internalization artifacts or on reference-only protocol rows that fail the protocol gate.

Thus the intrinsic candidate is the only candidate alive on both descended readout and signature-level descended update on the core surface.

paper_title: Internal Structure of a Surviving Promoted Package on Fixed Support in Six Birds Theory

name: Six mechanisms (P1--P6)
label: def:pvnp:six-mechanisms
compact: def:pvnp:six-mechanisms The saturated SAT shell carries the following six mechanisms. • \(P_1\), machine update. This is the deterministic polynomial-time transducer class admitted on the SAT layer, namely the class \(K_poly\) declared in the audited shell. Update is by lawful polynomial-time machine action on encoded SAT instances. • \(P_2\), admissibility. This is the set of encoded SAT instances admitted at the current finite stage. Admissibility is determined by the finite-stage restriction of the audited shell's instance database, together with the type-correctness and no-smuggling checks imposed by the lawfulness discipline. • \(P_3\), timescale. This is the polynomial budget declared by the lawful instrument \( \), including the local clock and the time certificate recorded by each lawful current observable. • \(P_4\), lens selection. This is the visibility lens of the audited shell, determining which projection of histories is exposed to current observation, and which wider projection is used for predictive observation. • \(P_5\), packaging. This is the \(Q/M\) quotient and continuation packaging: the SAT-saturated current and predictive quotients \( \) and \( \), together with the comparison map \( \) on the history carrier \( \). • \(P_6\), audit. This is the audit ledger of the audited shell, including the machine-index record, time certificate, replay log, and gate predicates declared in the audit interface. The closed audit record is part of the saturated SAT layer \( \), and the seven gates \(G_1\)--\(G_7\) are listed in app:gate-audit.

The check predicate says that the observable does not invoke an oracle for the SAT decision predicate. The status passes by construction: the audited shell admits ordinary deterministic polynomial-time transducers, not SAT-oracle machines. The evidence is the audit ledger recording the absence of oracle commitments. The implication is that the observable's computation does not implicitly use the SAT bit as input. • \( \), no witness oracle smuggling. The check predicate says that the observable does not invoke an oracle for a satisfying-witness producer . The status passes by construction, and the evidence is again the audit ledger of the admitted transducer. The check predicate says that the observable does not invoke an external NP-verifier oracle. The implication is that the observable cannot be a partial decider presented as a total current observable. • \( \), no overreading suppression. paper_title: Promotion Criteria and Surviving Packages on Fixed Support in Six Birds Theory
name: Candidate promoted package
label: def:candidate-promoted-package
compact: def:candidate-promoted-package Fix a common support surface together with a designated observable family and an admissible family of lower-layer operations. A candidate promoted package is an abstract package-level description intended to summarize lower-layer states or histories on that fixed-support surface. Its purpose is not merely to record a smaller state space but to provide a package on which the designated observables and admissible operations can be read without hidden dependence on arbitrary representatives. A candidate may be intrinsic, representative-selected, protocol-indexed, or otherwise structured, but it is always evaluated on the same frozen corpus and designated slice.

paper_title: Promotion Criteria and Surviving Packages on Fixed Support in Six Birds Theory
name: Induced update law
label: def:induced-update-law
compact: def:induced-update-law A candidate carries an induced update law when the admissible lower-layer operations act on the package in a well-defined way that does not depend on the choice of lower representative. If two lower states are identified by the candidate package, admissible continuations must not immediately reintroduce an unrecorded distinction at the package level. The induced update law is the package-level expression of descent from the lower surface.

paper_title: Promotion Criteria and Surviving Packages on Fixed Support in Six Birds Theory
name: Admissible second-stage coarse-graining
label: def:second-stage-coarse-graining
compact: def:second-stage-coarse-graining An admissible second-stage coarse-graining is a further package-level coarse-graining or repackaging that remains admissible relative to the retained observable surface and the induced update law. Not every quotient of the candidate is admissible; admissibility is tied to the structure the package is supposed to preserve. The identity coarse-graining is always admissible. The substantive question is whether nontrivial admissible further coarse-grainings exist and, if so, whether the decisive structure survives them.

paper_title: Promotion Criteria and Surviving Packages on Fixed Support in Six Birds Theory
name: Promoted-package criterion
label: def:promoted-package-criterion
compact: def:promoted-package-criterion A candidate package counts as a promoted package on the designated corpus and slice only if all of the following hold: [label=( )] • Sufficiency. The candidate supports the designated observable family on the frozen corpus. • Induced closure. The admissible lower-layer operations descend to a well-defined package-level update law. • Second-stage stability. The decisive structure survives admissible further coarse-graining, or else the candidate is rigid-minimal for explicit admissibility reasons rather than vacuous fragility. • Control admissibility. The candidate separates the required null, memory-only, artifact, and boundary-sensitive controls in the right way. • No-smuggling. The candidate's apparent success does not depend on omitted protocol or scheduler variables that should have been internalized. • Slice legibility. On at least one designated slice, the candidate is not merely sufficient but distinguished as a frontier-level package.

paper_title: Promotion Criteria and Surviving Packages on Fixed Support in Six Birds Theory
name: Protocol-indexed promotion
label: def:protocol-indexed-promotion
compact: def:protocol-indexed-promotion A distinct case occurs when promotion is available only after context or protocol state is internalized into the package. We call this protocol-indexed promotion. The base candidate does not qualify honestly on its own, because its apparent success depends on omitted protocol state, but an internalized or explicitly indexed version satisfies the promoted-package criterion once that dependence is represented inside the state object. This is stronger than a mere artifact diagnosis and weaker than intrinsic promotion: the route remains live, but only as an indexed package rather than as a context-free one.

paper_title: Promotion Criteria and Surviving Packages on Fixed Support in Six Birds Theory
name: Generic promotion criterion
label: prop:generic-promotion-criterion
compact: prop:generic-promotion-criterion Let a candidate package on fixed support be equipped with an induced update law. Suppose that, on the designated frozen corpus and slice, the candidate is sufficient for the observable family, satisfies the admissible second-stage stability condition, is control-admissible on the required controls, obeys the no-smuggling condition, and is slice-legible. Then the candidate satisfies the promoted-package criterion on that surface.

paper_title: Promotion Criteria and Surviving Packages on Fixed Support in Six Birds Theory
name: Intrinsic survivor on the flagship core
label: prop:intrinsic-main-result
compact: prop:intrinsic-main-result On the canonical promotion pipeline, the intrinsic route `P_int` survives on both Route A flagship anchors, remains separated from the required controls, and remains honest under the paired artifact audit. In this sense it is a surviving promoted-package route on the flagship core.

paper_title: Promotion Criteria and Surviving Packages on Fixed Support in Six Birds Theory
name: Secondary representative-selected survivors
label: prop:secondary-lift-survivors
compact: prop:secondary-lift-survivors On the Route A flagship core, the declared-completion family `P_decl` and the paired-enrichment family `P_pair` survive as representative-selected route-family results. name: Candidate promoted package
compact: Fix a common support surface, a designated observable family, and an admissible family of lower-level operations. name: Global nonclaims for the role architecture
label: rem:atlas-global-nonclaims
compact: rem:atlas-global-nonclaims The role architecture preserves the following nonclaims, all carried forward into the admissibility regime of Section sec:admissibility-meta-theory and the theorem chain of Sections sec:lower-bounds--sec:decomposition-exhaustion: [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • no full six-primitives algebra is claimed; • no global primitive-independence theorem is claimed; • no empirical realization is claimed; • no uniqueness of primitive presentations is claimed; • no uniqueness of selected lifts is claimed; • no lower-level-to-higher-level determinacy is claimed; • no instrument-free formulation is claimed; • direct cross-level comparison remains inadmissible without translation.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Admissible claim under honest bookkeeping
label: prop:honest-bookkeeping
compact: prop:honest-bookkeeping Honest bookkeeping is the admissibility regime for claims about a description \(D ∈ \). A claim that enters the theorem chain is declared admissible only if every assertion below carries an explicit record in \(D\): [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • the claim itself, with its statement, hypotheses, and scope; • every promotion, with its source level, target level, added data, losses, and preserved nonclaims; • every translation, with its source context, target context, preserved data, suppressed data, and claim strength; • every selected lift, marked selected and non-unique; • every forgetting map, with its record of losses; • every visibility claim, with both its visible and its suppressed data; • every empirical-bridge assertion, with its substrate, observable, instrument, level map, threshold-witness relation, and suppressed-structure nonclaims. Accordingly, unrecorded claims, implicit promotions, silent translations, asserted-but-unselected lifts, lossless forgetting without proof, visibility overreads, and bare empirical-realization assertions are all inadmissible.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Why the regime is necessary
label: rem:why-honest-bookkeeping
compact: rem:why-honest-bookkeeping The bookkeeping requirement is a structural check, not a stylistic one. Without explicit records, passive observation can be misread as , mere packaging as descent, and route failure as mismatch. The regime prevents those misreadings from entering the theorem chain.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Typed non-collapse
label: prop:typed-non-collapse
compact: prop:typed-non-collapse Under honest bookkeeping (Definition prop:honest-bookkeeping) and the repaired alignments of Remark rem:repaired-alignments, for every pair of primitive roles \((P_i, P_j)\) with \(i j\), the ``forbidden collapse'' of the corresponding row in Table tab:boundary-matrix is not admissible as an identification of \(P_i\) with \(P_j\); the ``permitted interaction'' of the same row is not thereby excluded and may remain admissible when its own bookkeeping conditions are met.Tracked in the formalization harness as a conditional schema (SixBirds.typed\_non\_collapse); see Appendix app:mechanization.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Typed non-collapse versus global independence
label: rem:typed-non-collapse-vs-independence
compact: rem:typed-non-collapse-vs-independence Typed non-collapse is strictly weaker than global primitive independence. It does not assert that the six roles are logically or categorically independent in a global algebra; it asserts only that the pairwise identifications listed as forbidden collapses in Table tab:boundary-matrix are inadmissible under honest bookkeeping, leaving the corresponding typed interactions available.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Level profile of an admissible claim
label: prop:level-profile
compact: prop:level-profile Every admissible claim about a description \(D ∈ \) carries a level profile: each claim is located on the behavioral, verification, or structural-categorical level, and each cross-level assertion is accompanied by a translation record in the sense of Definition prop:honest-bookkeeping. Direct comparison of claims at different levels without a translation record is inadmissible.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Admissible forgetting and selected lifts
label: prop:forgetting-lifts
compact: prop:forgetting-lifts Forgetting from the structural-categorical level to verification, and from verification to behavioral, is admissible and is always lossy in principle: an admissible forgetting carries a record of the losses in \(D\). Lifting from a lower level to a higher level is admissible only when accompanied by [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • the added data required to support the higher-level statement; • the mark that the lift is selected and non-unique; • explicit preservation of lower-level invariants and explicit losses where the lift is partial. Lossless forgetting and unique lifts are inadmissible unless the losslessness or uniqueness is itself proved and recorded.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Lower-to-higher non-determinacy
label: rem:lower-to-higher-non-determinacy
compact: rem:lower-to-higher-non-determinacy Definition prop:forgetting-lifts formalizes the non-determinacy of lower-level data: given behavioral or verification content alone, no choice of structural-categorical content is forced by the admissibility regime, and any asserted choice must be marked as a selected lift.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Activation thresholds
label: prop:activation-thresholds
compact: prop:activation-thresholds At the regime level, the threshold-attachment discipline of Definition def:threshold-attachment reads as follows. An admissible active derived role projection \( _i(D)\) exists only when \(D\) carries the threshold, witness, level, collapse, and audit data required by Definition def:threshold-attachment. Below-threshold clusters carry an explicit \( \) status, and boundary-collapsed clusters carry \( \). Arbitrary enrichment, adding structure solely to force a role projection, is inadmissible unless the additions are themselves honestly bookkept as raw features or annotations. This is a restatement of the attachment protocol at regime level and adds no content beyond Definition def:threshold-attachment.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Admissible visibility record
label: prop:visibility
compact: prop:visibility Every admissible claim carries an explicit visibility record comprising its visible content, its suppressed content, the instruments under which the visibility and suppression are asserted, and the resulting instrument-relative claim strength. Overreading a suppressed claim as visible under a different instrument is inadmissible. Partial visibility, in which a claim is visible only up to some coarsening or translation, is admitted when the visibility record itself makes the partiality explicit.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: No instrument-free truth
label: rem:no-instrument-free
compact: rem:no-instrument-free Definition prop:visibility does not claim that instruments are free of distortion or that any single instrument is canonical. It asserts only that admissible claims carry an instrument-relative visibility record. Instrument completeness is deferred to Section sec:future-work.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Admissible empirical-bridge claim
label: prop:empirical-bridge
compact: prop:empirical-bridge An empirical-bridge claim about \(D ∈ \) is admissible only when it carries, in \(D\), [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • the substrate and observable to which the bridge relates; • the instrument under which the observable is measured; • the level map between the closure-algebraic content and the substrate-level content; • a threshold-witness relation recording when the bridge is crossed; • the nonclaims suppressed by the bridge record, in particular any structural content of \(D\) that is not tracked by the substrate or instrument. Empirical realization --- the claim that \(D\) is itself a substrate observation --- is stronger than empirical-bridge admissibility and is not asserted by any empirical-bridge claim.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Admissibility-regime nonclaim closure
label: prop:nonclaim-closure
compact: prop:nonclaim-closure Under the admissibility regime, the following remain non-claims: [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • no full six-primitives algebra is claimed; • no global primitive-independence theorem is claimed; • no empirical realization is claimed; • no unique lift theorem is claimed; • no lower-level-to-higher-level determinacy is claimed; • no instrument-free truth claim is made; • direct cross-level comparison remains inadmissible without translation; • forgetting remains lossy unless losslessness is explicitly proved; • empirical-bridge claims require threshold data, level maps, instrument visibility records, and suppressed-structure nonclaims. Tracked in the formalization harness as a conditional schema (SixBirds.nonclaim\_closure); see Appendix app:mechanization.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Raw record
label: def:raw-record
compact: def:raw-record A raw record is a finite typed syntactic or relational feature of a description. The admissible record kinds are [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • object and state records; • relation records, map records, and partial-map records; • predicate records and comparison records; • path or derivation records; • index, order, transition, and refinement records; • trace, event, and provenance records; • replay and check records. A raw record is not, by itself, a -- role.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Annotations
label: def:annotations
compact: def:annotations In addition to raw records, a description admits annotations of six declared kinds: [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • level annotations \(Ann_L\); • threshold annotations \(Ann_ \); • lift annotations \(Ann_Lift\); • forgetting annotations \(Ann_Forget\); • instrument-visibility annotations \(Ann_Vis\); • empirical-bridge annotations \(Ann_Bridge\). These annotation kinds belong to the raw grammar; the finiteness and closure conditions on how they attach to declared records are imposed in the next subsection. For a description \(D\), we write \(D\) for the finite collection of raw records and annotations of \(D\).

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Independence of the feature alphabet
label: rem:alphabet-independence
compact: rem:alphabet-independence The record and annotation kinds in Definitions def:raw-record and def:annotations are syntactic or relational entities. No kind is named , , . Consequently, membership in does not require any derived role projection, does not require an exact-six decomposition/exhaustion record, and does not exclude candidate seventh-role features by definition. The role vocabulary will enter only in :derived-role-projections as a derived interpretation of raw features under threshold and witness data.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Finite description
label: def:finite
compact: def:finite A description \(D\) is finite when [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • \(D\) contains finitely many records and annotations; • every record or annotation carries finite typed fields; • every relation, map, path, trace, or annotation is finitely represented; • every reference in a record points to a declared finite record of \(D\); • no infinite semantic, probabilistic, topological, geometric, causal, optimization, or resource structure is admitted unless it is finitely represented and bookkept as a raw feature of \(D\).

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Closed description
label: def:closed
compact: def:closed A finite description \(D\) satisfies the closure condition \(D\) when [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • every source and target of every relation or map record is a declared record of \(D\); • every endpoint of every path or derivation record is a declared record of \(D\); • every index, transition, order, or refinement reference is a declared record of \(D\); • every trace, event, provenance, replay, or check record references declared records of \(D\); • every level, threshold, lift, forgetting, visibility, or empirical-bridge annotation references declared records of \(D\); • every claim carried by \(D\) has a bookkeeping record.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Audited description
label: def:audited
compact: def:audited A description \(D\) is audited when every claim carried by \(D\) has an honest bookkeeping record. The collection of such records is denoted \(D ⊆ D\), subject to the following discipline: [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • every promotion records its source level, target level, added data, losses, and nonclaims; • every translation records its source context, target context, preserved data, suppressed data, and claim strength; • every lift is marked as selected, not unique; • every forgetting map records its losses; • every visibility claim records both visible and suppressed data; • every empirical-bridge claim records substrate, observable, instrument, level map, threshold witness relation, and suppressed-structure nonclaims.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Finite audited typed closure description
label: def:fatcd
compact: def:fatcd A finite audited typed closure description is a finitely presented, closed, audited collection of typed raw records and annotations, equipped with honest bookkeeping for claims, levels, thresholds, visibility, forgetting, lifts, and empirical-bridge assertions where present. Equivalently, it is a description \(D\) whose raw content \(D\) is drawn from the kinds declared in Definitions def:raw-record and def:annotations, such that \(D\) is finite in the sense of Definition def:finite, satisfies the closure condition \(D\) of Definition def:closed, and is audited in the sense of Definition def:audited. We write for the class of all such descriptions, and \(D ∈ \) for membership.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: No minimum richness
label: rem:fatcd-minimality
compact: rem:fatcd-minimality imposes no lower bound on description size. A description consisting of a single object record together with the bookkeeping required by its claims may be admissible, as may a richer description carrying transitions, paths or derivations, annotations of every kind, and empirical-bridge annotations. The domain is defined by structural discipline, not by the presence of any particular feature kind.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Threshold attachment
label: def:threshold-attachment
compact: def:threshold-attachment A threshold annotation \(Ann_ ∈ D\) attaches first to a finite cluster \(C ⊆ D\) of raw features of \(D\), where \(C\) may consist of a single raw feature. No role projection is attempted on \(C\) until all of the following are present in \(D\): [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • the raw features of \(C\) themselves; • a threshold annotation \(Ann_ \) attached to \(C\); • a witness schema specifying what in \(C\) would support the attempted projection; • a record of the collapse cases that would invalidate the witness; • a level annotation \(Ann_L\) attached to \(C\); • an audit record in \(D\) honestly bookkeeping the claim.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Pre-projection discipline
label: rem:pre-projection
compact: rem:pre-projection The items of Definition def:threshold-attachment form a structural precondition, not a process narrative. What matters is that each item is present explicitly in \(D\) before a role projection is asserted, so that no threshold, witness, collapse case, or level is supplied tacitly by the act of projection itself.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Derived role projection
label: def:role-projection
compact: def:role-projection A derived role projection for a description \(D ∈ \) at role index \(i ∈ \1, ,6\\) is an active derived interpretation \( _i(D)\) of raw features of \(D\) as the role \(P_i\), supported by threshold data, witness schema, level assignment, and honest bookkeeping. Concretely, \( _i(D)\) is specified by [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • the proposed role name, one of , , , , , ; • a raw feature cluster \(C ⊆ D\) on which the role is interpreted; • the threshold data \( _i\) attached to \(C\) in the sense of Definition def:threshold-attachment; • a witness schema \(W_i\) specifying what constitutes a witness for the candidate role under its fixed meaning; • a level assignment \(Level_i\); • an evidence or certificate type; • a record of collapse cases avoided or accepted; • loss and lift annotations for any level crossings involved; • the explicit nonclaims preserved by the projection. The supporting data for \( _i(D)\) are carried by \(D\) and certified by \(D\) in the sense of Definition def:audited.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Fixed role meanings
label: rem:fixed-role-meanings
compact: rem:fixed-role-meanings The role names -- are defined by their meanings in Section sec:primitive-role-architecture: concerns update-vs-quotient compatibility and descent obstruction; concerns macro-specification representability; concerns enriched route and coherence mismatch, not a directionality certificate; concerns stage, order, transition, and refinement structure; concerns quotient packaging; and concerns audit, bookkeeping, provenance, replay, and checkability. The witness schema \(W_i\) in Definition def:role-projection must be aligned with these meanings; a cluster whose raw features do not support the meaning of the proposed role contributes no \( _i(D)\).

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Projection and membership are independent
label: rem:projection-vs-membership
compact: rem:projection-vs-membership Whether a description \(D\) supports a given derived role projection \( _i(D)\) is not part of the admissibility conditions of Definitions def:finite--def:audited. A description \(D ∈ \) may carry no derived role projection, projections for some roles, or projections for all six; its membership in is unaffected. The decomposition/exhaustion record of Section sec:decomposition-exhaustion accordingly assigns a status to every role channel of \(D\), only some of which need be active.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Residual feature; residual classification scheme
label: def:residual-scheme
compact: def:residual-scheme Let \(D ∈ \). A residual feature of \(D\) is a raw record or annotation in \(D\) whose role-theoretic disposition is not fixed solely by its raw-grammar kind. The residual classification scheme assigns to each residual feature \(r\) a single label \(Classify(r)\) drawn from the list [label=( ),topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • already absorbed into a derived -- projection \( _i(D)\); • composite of such projections; • presentation variant of an already classified feature; • level shift of an already classified feature; • activation-threshold refinement; • instrument-visibility artifact; • empirical-bridge annotation; • outside-domain structure; • already-covered bookkeeping or annotation data; • unresolved candidate seventh-role threat; • genuine seventh irreducible typed role. The scheme is declarative. At the domain-definition level, records the available labels but neither proves that every residual feature lands in categories (i)--(ix) nor proves that categories (x) and (xi) are empty. Those claims are deferred to Section sec:upper-bound-classification.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Optimization and objective data are not excluded
label: rem:optimization-not-excluded
compact: rem:optimization-not-excluded Raw features expressing optimization, objective, or selection criteria pass through the scheme of Definition def:residual-scheme; they are not dismissed by definition. Under the fixed role meanings (Remark rem:fixed-role-meanings), typical classifications include: a predicate or specification record possibly supporting a projection; a map or transition-selection record possibly supporting a or projection; a route-comparison or route-choice record possibly supporting a projection; an audit or check record possibly supporting a projection; an empirical-bridge annotation; or an outside-domain structure when the feature requires non-finite or unbookkept semantics. A feature that fits none of these is recorded under category (x).

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Non-circularity schema for
label: prop:non-circularity
compact: prop:non-circularity Membership in is not defined by requiring a decomposition/exhaustion record or by requiring any derived role projection to exist.Tracked in the formalization harness as a conditional schema (SixBirds.non\_circularity); see Appendix app:mechanization.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Non-overbreadth schema for
label: prop:non-overbreadth
compact: prop:non-overbreadth is structurally restricted and does not admit arbitrary syntactic material: arbitrary unaudited syntactic material cannot enter , and mentioning a role name without the supporting threshold, witness, level, collapse, and bookkeeping data does not by itself produce a derived role projection.Tracked in the formalization harness as a conditional schema (SixBirds.non\_overbreadth); see Appendix app:mechanization. The Lean declaration is identical in statement and proof to SixBirds.non\_circularity and re-extracts the admissibility fields of the record rather than establishing the structural-restriction content of the proposition.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Scoped exact-six question
label: def:scoped-exact-six-question
compact: def:scoped-exact-six-question The scoped exact-six question over asks whether, for every \(D ∈ \), there exists at least one decomposition/exhaustion record \(D\) whose role-channel structure consists of exactly the six typed closure-role channels , , , , , , each assigned exactly one of the five statuses later formalized in Section sec:decomposition-exhaustion, with all residual features of \(D\) classified under the scheme of Definition def:residual-scheme without recourse to categories (x) or (xi). No uniqueness is built into this question. The affirmative answer is denoted \(\), and is established in Section sec:scoped-exact-six conditionally on the recognition hypothesis introduced in Section sec:upper-bound-classification (Definition def:recognition-hypothesis), with the three principal threat classes settled unconditionally.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Channels, not active projections
label: rem:channel-vs-activation-reminder
compact: rem:channel-vs-activation-reminder An affirmative answer to the scoped exact-six question asserts the existence of six role channels per description, not six active derived projections per description. The distinction introduced in Remark rem:projection-vs-membership and formalized in Section sec:decomposition-exhaustion is preserved throughout.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Relation to the Foundations theorem
label: rem:fatcd-foundations-relation
compact: rem:fatcd-foundations-relation Proving \(\) is not a re-derivation of the canonical unavoidability result of Foundations I , and \(\) does not follow from that result alone. The Foundations theorem derives the -- vocabulary under minimal hypotheses of composability with limited interface access; the scoped exact-six claim asserts that, within the finite audited typed closure regime of and under the recognition hypothesis of Section sec:upper-bound-classification, every admissible description admits a six-channel decomposition/exhaustion record without a seventh irreducible typed role in the covered scope. The two results share vocabulary but address different questions.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Six-role lower bounds
label: thm:six-role-lower-bounds
compact: thm:six-role-lower-bounds For each role index \(i ∈ \1, ,6\\), there exists a description \(D_i ∈ \) and a derived active projection \( _i(D_i)\) witnessing the role channel \(P_i\) in the sense of Definition def:role-projection. In particular, each of , , , , , is instantiated by at least one admissible description in . This is an occurrence theorem, not an exhaustion theorem.Tracked in the formalization harness as a conditional schema (SixBirds.six\_role\_lower\_bounds); see Appendix app:mechanization.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Common witness data for role \(P_i\)
label: def:common-witness-data
compact: def:common-witness-data A witness of role \(P_i\) in is a tuple \[ (D_i, C_i, _i, W_i, Level_i, v_i^fin, v_i^cl, v_i^aud, n_i, _i(D_i) ) \] where [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • \(D_i ∈ \) is the ambient admissible description; • \(C_i ⊆ D_i\) is the raw feature cluster on which the projection is interpreted; • \( _i\) is the threshold annotation attached to \(C_i\); • \(W_i\) is the witness schema for the role meaning of \(P_i\) fixed in Definition def:primitive-roles; • \(Level_i\) is the level assignment in the sense of Definition def:level-trichotomy; • \(v_i^fin, v_i^cl, v_i^aud\) are the finite-description, closure, and audit/bookkeeping verifications for \(D_i\); • \(n_i\) is the explicit nonclaim record carried by the witness; • \( _i(D_i)\) is the derived role projection of Definition def:role-projection. A witness is admissible only if every item in this tuple is present and correctly aligned with the role meaning of \(P_i\).
