paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: What the lower bounds do and do not establish
label: rem:lower-bounds-scope
compact: rem:lower-bounds-scope Theorem thm:six-role-lower-bounds asserts that each of the six roles is instantiated somewhere in . It does not prove exact-six, does not rule out candidate seventh-role threats, does not prove decomposition, and does not prove uniqueness of any later decomposition/exhaustion record. It also does not assert that any single description activates all six channels simultaneously. Those questions are handled in Sections sec:upper-bound-classification and sec:decomposition-exhaustion.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Role-projection alignment
label: prop:alignment-rules
compact: prop:alignment-rules Under honest bookkeeping and the witness discipline of Definition def:common-witness-data, each role projection is constrained as follows. [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • : admissible only when the candidate cluster carries a selected update, a quotient or relation record, and a witness of descent compatibility, descent obstruction, or update-vs-quotient mismatch. Generic semantics, generic predicate meaning, generic selection criteria, and generic agency are not admissible as projections in the absence of such a witness. • : admissible only when the candidate carries a macro specification, a realization relation, specification-satisfaction data, and evidence of representability or non-representability. Macro-level predicates or objectives count only insofar as they are treated as content to be represented. Mere quotient equality, arbitrary relations without representability structure, and empirical observations without level and threshold data are not admissible as projections. • : admissible only when the candidate carries enriched route grammar, generated same-source, same-target route terms, and route-comparison data with a non-reducibility or coherence-mismatch certificate. Generic transitions, generic causal arrows, generic path records, and route undefinedness arising from obstruction are not admissible as projections unless the route/coherence threshold is explicitly present and the route comparison is specifically of the type. • : admissible only when the candidate carries a stage, order, transition, refinement, staged-dynamics, or regime-ordering record with laws beyond bare labels. Bare labels, arbitrary relations without order, transition, or refinement law, quotient packaging, and audit bookkeeping are not admissible as projections. • : admissible only when the candidate carries a quotient relation, a packaging map, the identification of distinct micro-elements, a same-package or quotient-object record, and quotient-validity evidence. Generic structural paths, derivations, topologies or geometries merely because they have paths, and causal chains are not admissible as projections unless quotient or packaging data is present. • : admissible only when the candidate carries an audit record with event reference, provenance or dependency trace, replay or check structure, and bookkeeping or checkability structure. Passive logs alone, arbitrary metadata, and certificate-only content without audit/provenance/replay/check structure are not admissible as projections. Tracked in the formalization harness as a conditional schema (SixBirds.alignment\_rules); see Appendix app:mechanization.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Three corrected alignments, held fixed
label: rem:three-repaired-alignments
compact: rem:three-repaired-alignments Proposition prop:alignment-rules fixes three alignments that are held throughout: generic transition data does not project to , generic path or derivation data does not project to , and generic semantic or interpretation data does not project to . These are carried into every step of the classification theorem below.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Closure of probability and uncertainty
label: prop:probability-closure
compact: prop:probability-closure Every admissible probability or uncertainty feature of a description \(D ∈ \) whose content takes one of the recognized forms below classifies, within the covered scope, as one of [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • a projection, when the feature is a macro-specification or representability condition; • a projection, when the feature is a stochastic transition or regime structure carrying valid stage or transition data; • a projection, when the feature is an audited uncertainty-bookkeeping record; • an activation-threshold refinement, when the uncertainty data modulates when an already admissible role projection activates without supplying a new witness schema; • an empirical-bridge annotation, when the feature expresses measurement uncertainty bridged to a substrate observable; • or a composite of the foregoing projections and annotations when the admissible bookkeeping carries several of these aspects at once. Probability or uncertainty content of any of these recognized forms therefore requires no seventh role; content of none of these forms is governed by the recognition hypothesis (Definition def:recognition-hypothesis).The Lean declaration is a trivial single-record harness check: classifyResidual maps RawKind.probability to composite, whose CoveredResidualClass branch is True; it does not establish the paper's universal probability/uncertainty closure. See Appendix app:mechanization (SixBirds.probability\_closure).

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Closure of residual causality
label: prop:causality-closure
compact: prop:causality-closure Every admissible residual-causality feature of a description \(D ∈ \) whose content takes one of the recognized forms below classifies, within the covered scope, as one of [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • a projection, as the primary classification when the feature is a directed transition, refinement, or staged-dependence record; • a projection, only when the feature is specifically a route/coherence comparison between generated same-source, same-target routes; • a projection, when the feature is a provenance or dependency audit; • a composite of and , when directed dependence and provenance audit occur together in the same admissible feature; • an outside-domain structure, when the feature requires metaphysical causation not amenable to honest bookkeeping. Classification as is inadmissible in the absence of quotient packaging. Residual-causality content of these recognized forms therefore requires no seventh role; content of none of these forms is governed by the recognition hypothesis (Definition def:recognition-hypothesis).The Lean declaration is a trivial single-record harness check: classifyResidual maps RawKind.causality to composite, whose CoveredResidualClass branch is True; the -inadmissibility content of the proposition is absent and no universal residual-causality closure is established. See Appendix app:mechanization (SixBirds.causality\_closure).

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Closure of residual agency
label: prop:agency-closure
compact: prop:agency-closure Every admissible residual-agency feature of a description \(D ∈ \) whose content takes one of the recognized forms below classifies, within the covered scope, as one of [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • a composite of , , and , when the feature decomposes into an objective or specification to be represented, a transition, regime, or staged selection event, and an audited decision-provenance record; • an empirical-bridge annotation, when observed agency serves as substrate evidence for a bridged claim; • an outside-domain structure, when irreducible intentional or teleological content is asserted beyond what admissible bookkeeping reduces to , , and . Classification as is inadmissible in the absence of an explicit update-vs-quotient descent obstruction. Residual-agency content of these recognized forms therefore requires no seventh role; content of none of these forms is governed by the recognition hypothesis (Definition def:recognition-hypothesis).The Lean declaration is a trivial single-record harness check: classifyResidual maps RawKind.agency to empiricalBridgeAnnotation, whose CoveredResidualClass branch is True; the -inadmissibility content is absent and no universal residual-agency closure is established. See Appendix app:mechanization (SixBirds.agency\_closure).

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Scope of the closures
label: rem:threat-closures-scope
compact: rem:threat-closures-scope Propositions prop:probability-closure--prop:agency-closure close the three threats within the covered scope; they do not make scope-free claims. A feature that falls outside the covered scope is classified as an outside-domain structure via Definition def:residual-scheme, not absorbed into a primitive role by default.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Recognition hypothesis
label: def:recognition-hypothesis
compact: def:recognition-hypothesis A description \(D ∈ \) satisfies the recognition hypothesis when every residual feature \(r ∈ D\) is recognized: the closure content of \(r\) either supplies the witness type of one of the six role meanings of Definition def:primitive-roles --- so that \(r\), or a finite composite of its constituents, projects to , , under Proposition prop:alignment-rules --- or instantiates one of the six annotation kinds of Definition def:annotations, or is substrate already accounted for by the audit discipline of . Equivalently, \(D\) carries no finite audited residual feature whose closure content is irreducible to the six role meanings, and in particular none whose role-theoretic content emerges only in an assembled cluster and is not the join of its constituents' role labels.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: The recognition hypothesis is assumed, not derived
label: rem:recognition-open
compact: rem:recognition-open The recognition hypothesis is an explicit assumption on \(D\), not a consequence of the definitions. Two kinds of finite, audited, in-domain feature are not known to be recognized: a feature carrying a conservation or balance law over declared records --- a finite resource invariant of the kind admitted by Definition def:finite --- whose content supplies none of the six witness types, and a feature whose closure content is an emergent obstruction or holonomy of an assembled cluster, not reducible to the role labels of its constituents. Whether every finite audited feature is recognized --- equivalently, whether the six roles are recognition-complete for --- is left open and is recorded with the endogenous-instrument meta-limit of Sections subsec:meta-limit and subsec:future-meta-limit. The three threat closures of Propositions prop:probability-closure--prop:agency-closure establish the recognition hypothesis unconditionally for the three highest-priority threat classes; the classification theorem below assumes it in general.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Upper-bound classification
label: thm:upper-bound-classification
compact: thm:upper-bound-classification Let \(D ∈ \) satisfy the recognition hypothesis (Definition def:recognition-hypothesis), and let \(r\) be a residual feature of \(D\) in the sense of Definition def:residual-scheme. Then \(r\) classifies as one of [label=( ),topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • already absorbed into an admissible , , , , , or projection under the alignment rules of Proposition prop:alignment-rules; • a composite of such projections; • a presentation variant of an already classified feature; • a level shift of an already classified feature; • an activation-threshold refinement; • an instrument-visibility artifact; • an empirical-bridge annotation; • an outside-domain structure; • already-covered bookkeeping or annotation data. Equivalently, within the covered scope, categories (x) and (xi) of Definition def:residual-scheme, namely the unresolved-threat and genuine-seventh-role categories, are empty: no covered candidate seventh-role feature remains as an unresolved threat, and no covered candidate seventh-role feature requires a genuine seventh irreducible typed closure role.The Lean declaration is a classifier-by-construction check: every RawKind branch of classifyResidual lands in a class whose CoveredResidualClass branch is True, and the uncovered constructors unresolvedThreat/genuineSeventhRole are never produced; ``no seventh role'' holds by construction rather than by derivation from feature content. See Appendix app:mechanization (SixBirds.upper\_bound\_classification).

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Scope of the theorem
label: rem:classification-scope
compact: rem:classification-scope Theorem thm:upper-bound-classification is conditional on the recognition hypothesis (Definition def:recognition-hypothesis) and scoped to . It does not derive that no finite audited feature requires a seventh role; it assumes this, and discharges the assumption unconditionally only for the three threat classes of Propositions prop:probability-closure--prop:agency-closure. It does not claim that no seventh role can arise outside , that the alignment rules are exhaustive for richer domains, or that the recognition hypothesis holds in general. Nor does it prove exact-six on its own: the decomposition/exhaustion theorem of Section sec:decomposition-exhaustion remains necessary. The open recognition-completeness question and broader questions are deferred to Sections subsec:meta-limit and sec:future-work.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Channel status
label: def:channel-status
compact: def:channel-status For each \(i ∈ \1, ,6\\), the role channel \(iD\) of a description \(D ∈ \) is the \(P_i\)-labeled slot in the six-channel interface associated to \(D\), regardless of whether that slot is active. A channel status for \(iD\) is exactly one of the five values [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • \( \) --- an active derived role projection \( _i(D)\) in the sense of Definition def:role-projection exists, with the full attachment data of Definition def:threshold-attachment; • \( \) --- candidate raw features are present but the threshold data required by Definition def:threshold-attachment is absent; • \( \) --- the candidate cluster is a boundary case that collapses under the witness schema \(W_i\); • \( \) --- no relevant raw features for role \(P_i\) are present in \(D\), and the absence is itself recorded; • \( \) --- the role-\(P_i\) content of \(D\) lies outside the covered scope. We write \(iD\) for the channel status of \(iD\).

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Decomposition/exhaustion record
label: def:decomposition-record
compact: def:decomposition-record A decomposition/exhaustion record for \(D ∈ \) is a tuple \[ D = (D, (iD, iD)_i=1^6, D, Classify, L, V, D, N ) \] where [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • the six role channels together with their statuses form the six-channel status sequence. If \(iD = \), the channel carries an active projection \( _i(D)\) with its full attachment data. If \(iD\) is inactive, the channel carries the corresponding below-threshold, collapsed-boundary, absent-with-record, or outside-scope status record; • \(D ⊆ D\) is the residual feature set (the raw records and annotations not already accounted for by an active projection or an inactive status record), and \(Classify\) assigns to each \(r ∈ D\) a label in the scheme of Definition def:residual-scheme; • \(L\) collects the loss and lift records for any level crossings involved in projections or classifications; • \(V\) collects instrument-visibility and empirical-bridge annotations where these are asserted; • \(D\) is the honest bookkeeping subrecord; • \(N\) is the explicit nonclaim record. A decomposition/exhaustion record is well-formed when each \(iD\) is drawn from the five values of Definition def:channel-status, each active \( _i(D)\) is admissible in the sense of Definitions def:role-projection and def:threshold-attachment, each inactive status record is honestly supported by the corresponding raw-feature situation, and every raw feature is accounted for at the channel/exhaustion level either by an active projection, by a status record for its channel, or by a residual classification. The records in \(L\) and \(V\) are auxiliary annotations on this coverage, not additional role channels.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Decomposition existence
label: thm:decomposition-existence
compact: thm:decomposition-existence Every description \(D ∈ \) admits a well-formed decomposition/exhaustion record \(D\) in the sense of Definition def:decomposition-record.Tracked in the formalization harness as a conditional schema (SixBirds.decomposition\_existence); see Appendix app:mechanization.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Six-channel exactness and residual exhaustion
label: thm:six-channel-exactness
compact: thm:six-channel-exactness For every \(D ∈ \) and every well-formed \(D\) in the sense of Definition def:decomposition-record: [label=( ),topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • the channel sequence \((iD)_i=1^6\) has length exactly six, one per primitive role , , ; • every raw feature of \(D\) is accounted for at the channel/exhaustion level by an active projection \( _i(D)\), a channel-status record for an inactive channel, or a residual classification under the scheme of Definition def:residual-scheme; the records in \(L\) and \(V\) are auxiliary annotations on this coverage; • under the recognition hypothesis (Definition def:recognition-hypothesis) and within the covered scope, no raw feature is classified as an unresolved seventh-role threat or as a genuine seventh irreducible typed closure role (Theorem thm:upper-bound-classification); the three principal threat classes are closed unconditionally. Tracked in the formalization harness as a conditional schema (SixBirds.six\_channel\_exactness); see Appendix app:mechanization.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Channel-versus-activation discipline
label: prop:channel-vs-activation
compact: prop:channel-vs-activation Let \(D ∈ \) and let \(D\) be a well-formed decomposition/exhaustion record. The following are distinct statements: [label=( ),topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • Six channels: the channel sequence \((iD)_i=1^6\) has length six with the fixed role names , , . • Six active projections: for each \(i\), \(iD = \) and the channel carries an active \( _i(D)\). Theorem thm:six-channel-exactness establishes (i) for every \(D ∈ \). It does not establish (ii). paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Decomposition records are not unique
label: prop:non-uniqueness
compact: prop:non-uniqueness A description \(D ∈ \) may admit more than one well-formed decomposition/exhaustion record in the sense of Definition def:decomposition-record. Distinct well-formed records may differ in level assignments, choice of witness schema, residual classification labels for features admitting more than one admissible category under the alignment rules, or placement of loss/lift and visibility records. Theorems thm:decomposition-existence and thm:six-channel-exactness assert existence, not uniqueness.The Lean development exhibits two concrete decomposition records of a single description that differ only in their P1 channel status; the Lean statement does not assert that either record is well-formed, and the further sources of non-uniqueness in the prose (level assignments, witness-schema choice, residual labels, loss/lift placement) are not mechanized. The narrowing is recorded in Appendix app:mechanization (SixBirds.non\_uniqueness).

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: What the decomposition theorems do and do not prove
label: rem:dec-scope
compact: rem:dec-scope Theorems thm:decomposition-existence and thm:six-channel-exactness establish the structural side of the scoped exact-six claim: every \(D ∈ \) admits a six-channel decomposition/exhaustion record, with residual exhaustion in the covered scope under the recognition hypothesis (Definition def:recognition-hypothesis). Together with the lower-bound theorem (Section sec:lower-bounds) and the upper-bound classification (Section sec:upper-bound-classification), they prepare the scoped exact-six theorem but do not replace the integrated-stress check that follows. They do not assert that every description activates all six roles, that the decomposition is canonical or unique, or that the scoped exact-six program extends beyond ; those remain nonclaims.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Dependency stress
label: prop:dependency-stress
compact: prop:dependency-stress The scoped exact-six target is dependency-coherent only when the theorem chain is assembled in the order \[ domain lower bounds upper-bound classification decomposition/exhaustion. \] Accordingly, the following are inadmissible: [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • asserting the target without the domain of Section sec:fatcd-domain; • asserting the target without the lower-bound theorem of Section sec:lower-bounds; • asserting the target without the upper-bound classification theorem of Section sec:upper-bound-classification; • asserting the target without the decomposition and exhaustion theorems of Section sec:decomposition-exhaustion; • promoting the assembled target before the integrated stress check of Proposition thm:integrated-stress.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Circularity stress
label: prop:circularity-stress
compact: prop:circularity-stress Three circularity patterns are inadmissible under the theorem chain: [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • redefining so that it already contains exactly six role slots by construction; • declaring the absence of a seventh role by definition rather than by classification under Definition def:residual-scheme; • justifying decomposition existence by assuming scoped exact-six. The non-circularity schema of Proposition prop:non-circularity and the constructive proof of Theorem thm:decomposition-existence block each pattern.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Channel-versus-activation stress
label: prop:channel-activation-stress
compact: prop:channel-activation-stress The following conflations are inadmissible: [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • requiring that every \(D ∈ \) activates all six role channels; • treating an inactive channel of status \( \) as an active witness for its role; • treating an inactive channel of status \( \) as an active witness; • treating an inactive channel of status \( \) as an active witness. Proposition prop:channel-vs-activation enforces each distinction. The same inactive-status guardrail also applies to \( \).

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Role-alignment stress
label: prop:role-alignment-stress
compact: prop:role-alignment-stress The three forbidden assignments of Remark rem:three-repaired-alignments are inadmissible: generic transition data does not project to , generic path or derivation data does not project to , and generic semantic or interpretation data does not project to . The alignment rules of Proposition prop:alignment-rules enforce each prohibition.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Upper-bound residual stress
label: prop:residual-stress
compact: prop:residual-stress Under Theorem thm:upper-bound-classification and within the covered scope, the following regressions are inadmissible: [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • probability or uncertainty features reopening as unresolved threats; • residual-causality features reopening as unresolved threats; • residual-agency features reopening as unresolved threats; • any covered residual feature remaining unclassified under Definition def:residual-scheme; • any covered residual feature requiring a genuine seventh irreducible typed closure role. Propositions prop:probability-closure--prop:agency-closure settle the three threat closures, and Theorem thm:upper-bound-classification, under the recognition hypothesis, delivers the emptiness of categories (x) and (xi).

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Overclaim stress
label: prop:overclaim-stress
compact: prop:overclaim-stress The following restatements of the scoped exact-six target are inadmissible: [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • restatement as a full six-primitives algebra; • restatement as a global primitive-independence theorem; • restatement as unique or canonical decomposition; • restatement as empirical realization; • restatement as a claim about all emergence phenomena, or any domain broader than . Remark rem:atlas-global-nonclaims, Proposition prop:nonclaim-closure, and Proposition prop:non-uniqueness carry the corresponding nonclaims forward through the theorem chain. In particular, nonclaim closure survives the exact-six assembly.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Integrated stress certification
label: thm:integrated-stress
compact: thm:integrated-stress The theorem chain of Sections sec:fatcd-domain, sec:lower-bounds, sec:upper-bound-classification, and sec:decomposition-exhaustion satisfies each of the six stress families recorded in the stress remarks of this section. Dependency, circularity, channel-versus-activation, role-alignment, upper-bound residual, and overclaim regressions are all blocked, and the assembled target is ready for the terminal statement of Section sec:scoped-exact-six.Tracked in the formalization harness as a conditional schema (SixBirds.integrated\_stress) bundling the six stress conjuncts; see Appendix app:mechanization.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations II: — [4pt] Admissibility, Meta-Theory, and the Exact-Six Program
name: Scoped exact-six
label: thm:scoped-exact-six
compact: thm:scoped-exact-six Let \(D ∈ \) satisfy the recognition hypothesis (Definition def:recognition-hypothesis). Then \(D\) admits a well-formed decomposition/exhaustion record \(D\) with exactly six typed closure-role channels: [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • : update-vs-quotient compatibility / descent obstruction; • : macro-specification representability; • : enriched route/coherence mismatch; • : stage/order/transition/refinement structure; • : quotient packaging / quotienting; • : audit/bookkeeping/provenance/replay/checkability. Each channel carries exactly one recorded status from \(\ , , , , \\). Every active projection is supported by threshold data, a witness schema, a level assignment, and an honest bookkeeping record. Every residual raw feature of \(D\) is classified, under the upper-bound classification of Section sec:upper-bound-classification, as one of: [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] • composite of existing role channels; • presentation variant; • level shift; • activation-threshold refinement; • instrument-visibility artifact; • empirical-bridge annotation; • outside-domain structure; • already-covered bookkeeping or annotation data. Under that hypothesis, no residual feature remains as an unresolved candidate seventh role or genuine seventh irreducible typed closure role; for the three principal threat classes --- probability, causality, and agency --- this holds unconditionally (Propositions prop:probability-closure--prop:agency-closure). We denote this conclusion by \[ . \]Tracked in the formalization harness as a conditional schema (SixBirds.scoped\_exact\_six); see Appendix app:mechanization.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations IV: — A Catalog of Layer-Agnostic Structural Laws
name: Closure formation
label: def:closure-formation
compact: def:closure-formation A closure formation is the passage from initial data to the object obtained by closing that data under a declared family of closure rules. We write \( \) for the formed-closure operation. A formed closure is the completed object relative to the declared rules. A closure-of-record is a formed closure together with an audit record of the closure data used to form it.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations IV: — A Catalog of Layer-Agnostic Structural Laws
name: Current and predictive quotients
label: def:quotient-packaging
compact: def:quotient-packaging Quotient packaging is the standard quotient construction: an equivalence relation is imposed on a carrier and only equivalence classes are retained. The quotient map is denoted \( \) when no more specific symbol is needed. The current quotient \( \) is the quotient presently visible to the apparatus. The predictive quotient \( \) is a finer quotient predicted by the apparatus but not necessarily visible at the current level. Thus \( \) refines \( \): a \( \)-class may contain several \( \)-classes.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations IV: — A Catalog of Layer-Agnostic Structural Laws
name: BirdInt judgment
label: def:birdint
compact: def:birdint A \( \) judgment is the \ finite audited interaction judgment. In this paper it records that the interaction named in a catalog law is legitimately observable by the declared finite audit data. It is not an informal plausibility assertion; it is the inherited finite-witness condition for observable interaction.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations IV: — A Catalog of Layer-Agnostic Structural Laws
name: Split-pair obstruction
label: def:split-pair
compact: def:split-pair Let \(q:X→ Q\) be a source quotient, \(F:X→ Y\) a map, and \(r:Y→ R\) a target identification. The split-pair obstruction is \[ (q,F,r) = \(x,x')∈ X× X q(x)=q(x')\ and\ rF(x) rF(x')\. \] It is the set of pairs identified by the source quotient but separated after transport to the target quotient.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations IV: — A Catalog of Layer-Agnostic Structural Laws
name: Observation signature; access quotient
label: def:access-quotient
compact: def:access-quotient An observation signature is a declared map \( :H→ \) from a carrier \(H\) to observation symbols. It determines the access kernel \[ h _I h' (h)= (h'). \] The access quotient \( \) is the quotient of \(H\) by this kernel. It is the quotient carrying exactly the distinctions made by the declared observation signature.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations IV: — A Catalog of Layer-Agnostic Structural Laws
name: Normal-form template
label: def:normal-form
compact: def:normal-form Each catalog law is presented by a six-part normal-form template: setup, theorem, proof spine, case enumeration, interaction status, and nonclaims. The setup names the data on which the law operates. The theorem states the layer-agnostic claim. The proof spine gives the structural argument. The case enumeration lists the mutually exclusive outcomes when the statement branches. The interaction status records the relevant \( \) legitimacy condition. The nonclaims field states what the law does not assert. fig:normal-form-template gives the schematic form.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations IV: — A Catalog of Layer-Agnostic Structural Laws
name: Observation signature
label: def:obs-signature

Its access kernel is the equivalence relation \[ h _I h' (h)= (h'), \] and its access quotient is the quotient map \[ :H→ Q_I:=H/ _I. \] For a calibration family of observation signatures, the same construction is applied to the joint access kernel.

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations IV: — A Catalog of Layer-Agnostic Structural Laws

paper_title: Six Birds Foundations IV: — A Catalog of Layer-Agnostic Structural Laws

label: thm:F12
compact: thm:F12 A functorial gate using only the existing access quotient cannot produce a strict new current distinction. If a readout \(d:H→ D\) is current-visible without additional apparatus data, then \[ _dist( ,d)= , equivalently d= d \] for some \( d:Q_I→ D\). paper_title: Six Birds Foundations IV: — A Catalog of Layer-Agnostic Structural Laws
name: Hiddenness interface
label: def:hiddenness-exposure

name: E12.1: Operational selfhood (unformalized)
label: rem:e12-selfhood
compact: rem:e12-selfhood At the cognitive scale, take role, memory, action, and viability as the declared domains whose future probes must be jointly supported. The source program calls a self the private common repair ledger \(L_S\) through which those cross-domain probes jointly descend. ``Private'' here means carried by the selected system and available to its own repair interfaces; it does not mean phenomenally private or inaccessible in principle. The object of the claim is the ledger and its factorization property, not an inner observer. The specialization turns the Foundations IV F17 common-quotient idea inward. F17 compares observations across public viewpoints; E12.1 compares the system's own role, record, action, and viability interfaces. When one versioned ledger supplies the distinctions used by all four interfaces, the same repair occurrence can be traced across them. When the ledger is lost or fragmented, histories may remain equal under an action quotient while their memory or role futures differ, or equal under a role quotient while their viability futures differ. Those are ordinary cross-domain split pairs, not a metaphysical failure of identity. The corresponding falsifier is therefore operational. A selfhood claim fails if the proposed \(L_S\) is not carried, if one declared domain does not factor through it, if a cross-domain repair borrows an external or wrong-lineage record, or if fragmentation is claimed without a literal split pair between two of the declared future readouts. A perfectly integrated ledger can also fail E12 individuation when its budget, boundary, or repair apparatus is maintained by another carrier. The current development has no theorem constructing \(L_S\), no exhaustive inventory of cognitive domains, and no consciousness consequence. E12.1 is not used by a later proof.

paper_title: Six Birds: — Foundations of Emergence Calculus
name: Interoperability of certificates (toolkit safety)
label: rem:tk-interoperability
compact: rem:tk-interoperability This manuscript uses three logically distinct ``certificate families'': stability (existence/robustness of fixed points of a completion rule), novelty (strict theory extension by adding non-definable predicates), and directionality (nontrivial audit values such as affinities or path reversal asymmetry). They are intentionally separated to prevent accidental overinterpretation. The three certificate families (Stability, Novelty, Directionality) are logically independent. Each can hold or fail independently of the others. The only designed interactions are: (C1) completion defines stable objects, (C2) extension changes definability, (C3) audit is monotone under coarse-graining. No other implications are intended or valid. Non-implications. • Stability (small idempotence defect / approximate closure) does not imply novelty: a system may stabilize within a fixed definability structure (Section sec:idempotent-endo) without any strict theory extension (Section sec:forcing). • Novelty does not imply directionality: adding a generic predicate (Section sec:forcing) can change what is expressible while leaving the audit certificates unchanged. • Stability and novelty do not imply directionality: directionality is certified only by the audit functional and its monotonicity laws (Sections sec:acc and sec:aot). No false positives for directionality under observation. Coarse-graining cannot create arrow-of-time: the path reversal asymmetry contracts under pushforward (data processing in Section sec:aot). Apparent irreversibility caused by hiding an internal protocol/phase is diagnosed by the protocol-trap/clock-audit pattern (Section sec:aot). Where coupling actually occurs. The only intended coupling mechanisms are explicit operators: (i) completion changes fixed-point sets (Sections sec:closure and sec:idempotent-endo), (ii) extension refines definability (Section sec:forcing), and (iii) the audit functional is functorial/monotone under lenses (Sections sec:acc and sec:aot). Appendix E's ECT template is an optional coupling that links completion/accounting to a throughput/capacity certificate under explicit slots; it still does not certify novelty or directionality. Appendix E's balanced-atom route (Definitions def:ect-atom-ss--def:ect-bal and Corollary cor:ect-bal-icap) is one optional way to couple packaging/accounting to a throughput certificate; it still does not certify novelty (Section sec:forcing) or directionality (Sections sec:acc--sec:aot). Route dependence (holonomy) is treated separately as a reduction-order effect and is not, by itself, a directionality certificate.

paper_title: Six Birds: — Foundations of Emergence Calculus
name: Emergence and open-endedness (terminology)
compact: Throughout, emergence means the appearance of stable fixed points of a completion rule within a theory package, while open-endedness means strict theory extension (a change in definability or completion), not iteration of a fixed closure. paper_title: Six Birds: — Foundations of Emergence Calculus
name: Finite theory package
label: def:tk-theory-package
compact: def:tk-theory-package Assume A\_FIN. A finite theory package is a tuple \[ T = (Z,\ f,\ _f,\ E,\ A) \] where: • `Z` is a finite carrier set (microstate space). • `f:Z→ X` is a lens (coarse description). The induced definability structure ` _f` is the finite ` `-algebra (equivalently, partition) on `Z` generated by `f`, i.e.\ the family of predicates measurable with respect to `f`. • `E: V→ V` is a completion/packaging endomap on a chosen space of descriptions ` V` associated to `Z`. Typically `E` is idempotent (`E E=E`) or approximately idempotent in a specified norm. In the empirical/dynamical instantiation ` V= (Z)`, while in the order-theoretic instantiation ` V=Z` (with `E` a closure operator). • ` A` is an audit functional (a certificate of directionality or drive) defined on the relevant objects in context (e.g.\ path laws for a Markov dynamics, or antisymmetric edge 1-forms on a support graph), together with a designated monotonicity principle under coarse observation: for any further coarsening `g:X→ Y`, the induced pushforward should not increase the audit, schematically \[ A ((g f)_\#( ) )\ \ A (f_\#( ) ), \] whenever both sides are defined. We call ` _f` the expressive content of the theory and `E` its completion rule; the fixed points of `E` are the internally complete descriptions/objects recognized by the theory at the chosen scale and lens.

paper_title: Six Birds: — Foundations of Emergence Calculus
name: Instantiations in this manuscript
label: rem:tk-theory-instantiations
compact: rem:tk-theory-instantiations The components of ` T` appear throughout the paper in specialized forms. In Section sec:closure, an order-closure operator `c` on a poset is an idempotent completion rule; fixed points of `c` are the ``objects'' at that rung of a closure ladder. In Section sec:idempotent-endo, we isolate idempotent endomaps as the minimal abstraction behind this fixed-point viewpoint. In Section sec:idempotent-endo we also construct, from a Markov kernel, a lens `f`, and a timescale, a dynamics-induced completion endomap `E_ ,f` on ` (Z)`. In Section sec:forcing, adjoining a new predicate corresponds to refining ` _f` to a strictly stronger definability structure, i.e.\ a theory extension. Finally, Sections sec:acc and sec:aot provide two audit families used here: graph 1-form exactness/affinities (ACC) and path reversal asymmetry (arrow-of-time), the latter enjoying a precise monotonicity principle under coarse-graining (data processing).

name: Closure operator
label: def:closure-operator
compact: def:closure-operator Let `(L, )` be a poset. A map `c:L→ L` is a closure operator if for all `x,y∈ L`: • (Extensive) `x c(x)`. • (Monotone) `x y c(x) c(y)`. • (Idempotent) `c(c(x)) = c(x)`.

paper_title: Six Birds: — Foundations of Emergence Calculus

label: def:closure-ladder
compact: def:closure-ladder A closure ladder is a sequence of closure operators `(c_n)_n∈ N` on `L` such that `c_n c_n+1` for all `n`. The fixed-point sets form a nested chain \[ Fix(c_0) Fix(c_1) Fix(c_2) \] by Lemma lem:closed-antitone.

paper_title: Six Birds: — Foundations of Emergence Calculus
compact: The strictness relation ` ` is irreflexive and transitive on closure operators (by the pointwise order), and Lemma lem:closed-antitone records the antitone behavior of fixed points. On a fixed finite lattice, any ` `-chain is finite; the open-endedness modeled here comes from changing the theory/closure package or enlarging domains, not from a single finite lattice. Viewed abstractly, a closure operator acts like a completion rule. Iterating a fixed completion rule stabilizes. In a poset, closure operators correspond to reflections onto their fixed points (see Remark rem:lean-closure).

name: Idempotent endomap
compact: Let `A` be a set (or type). An idempotent endomap on `A` is a function `e : A → A` such that `e e = e`, i.e.\ `e(e(a)) = e(a)` for all `a∈ A`.

name: Fixed points
compact: For an endomap `e : A → A` define its fixed-point set \[ Fix(e) := \a∈ A : e(a)=a\. \] We interpret `Fix(e)` as the collection of ``objects'' completed by `e`.

Then `r i = id_Fix(e)` and `i r = e`. In particular, `e` restricts to the identity on `Fix(e)` and `Fix(e)` canonically identifies with the image of `e`.

paper_title: Six Birds: — Foundations of Emergence Calculus
name: Order-closures as a special case
compact: If `L` is a poset and `c:L→ L` is an order-closure (extensive, monotone, idempotent), then forgetting the order yields an idempotent endomap on the underlying set. The converse is false: an idempotent endomap need not be monotone or extensive with respect to any nontrivial order. In particular, the dynamics-induced operators `E_ ,f` (defined later on probability simplices) are treated as (approximate) idempotent endomaps with fixed points and idempotence defects measured in a chosen metric, rather than as order-closures. We will sometimes call an idempotent endomap a semantic completion map for a theory: its fixed points are the internally complete descriptions with respect to that completion.

name: Protocol trap / hidden-drive principle (T-AOT-02)
label: thm:protocol_trap
compact: thm:protocol_trap Assume A\_FIN+A\_AUT. Suppose: (i) the phase chain ` S` is reversible with stationary distribution `s`; (ii) each `K_ ` is reversible with respect to a common stationary distribution ` ` on `X`. Then the product measure ` := × s` is stationary for the lifted chain on `Z=X× ` and the lifted chain is reversible (hence ` _T( )=0` for all `T`). Consequently, by Theorem thm:dpi_path applied to the projection `X× → X`, the observed process on `X` has zero path reversal asymmetry at every finite horizon. In particular, any apparent arrow-of-time obtained by analysing a stroboscopic composition of kernels on `X` must be traced to either: (a) an external schedule (violating A\_AUT), or (b) a driven/bias phase dynamics (nonzero affinity, cf.\ Section sec:acc).

For any stationary distribution of the lifted autonomous chain, nonzero steady-state entropy production requires a nontrivial affinity component (P6\_drive) in the lifted dynamics (e.g.\ a biased phase cycle) or an external schedule.

paper_title: Six Birds: — Foundations of Emergence Calculus
name: What the ``protocol trap'' actually warns about
compact: The theorem above is about true path reversal asymmetry. In practice, one can still obtain a spurious ``arrow'' by fitting a one-step Markov model to a non-Markov observed process (for example, by replacing the hidden-phase model by a stroboscopic kernel on `X`). The cure is the clock audit: include the phase variable in the state, or work directly with path-space quantities that do not assume Markovianity at the observed level.

name: Predicates and definability
compact: A (Boolean) predicate is a function `h:Z→\0,1\`. We say that `h` is definable from the theory `f` (equivalently: ` _f`-measurable) if it is constant on each block: \[ x∈ X,\ z,z'∈ B_x, h(z)=h(z'). \] Equivalently, there exists ` h:X→\0,1\` with `h= h f`.

paper_title: Six Birds: — Foundations of Emergence Calculus
compact: In a fixed finite `Z` there is a hard cap on how many strict refinements are possible; open-endedness is modeled by repeated extensions across growing problems/domains (each step finite). The ``finite forcing lemma'' is a combinatorial proxy and does not claim set-theoretic independence.

compact: Assume A\_FIN+A\_LENS and let `f:Z→ X` have blocks ` _f=\B_x\_x∈ X`. For each block `B_x`, \[ P(h is constant on B_x)=2^1-|B_x|, \] and by a union bound, \[ P( x∈ X such that h is constant on B_x)\ \ _x∈ X 2^1-|B_x|. \] In particular, if every block has size at least `m 2`, then \[ P(h splits every block) \ \ 1 - K 2^1-m. \]

name: Generic extension is strict
label: cor:strict-language-extension
compact: cor:strict-language-extension Assume A\_FIN+A\_LENS. With probability `1-2^-(N-K)`, the refined lens `(f,h):Z→ X×\0,1\` is a strict refinement of `f`. Equivalently, it distinguishes at least one pair of microstates previously indistinguishable under `f`.

paper_title: Six Birds: — Foundations of Emergence Calculus
name: Why this is the anti-saturation move
compact: Closure (or packaging) at a fixed theory saturates by idempotence: repeated closure steps do not create an infinite strict chain. Corollary cor:strict-language-extension exhibits a mathematically clean extension step: adjoining a generic predicate changes the theory itself in a way that is overwhelmingly not reconstructible from the old distinctions. This is the finite “forcing-style” mechanism we use to justify strict ladder climbing via theory/completion change.

paper_title: Six Birds: — Foundations of Emergence Calculus
name: Process soup (D-META-PROC-01)
label: def:meta-proc
compact: def:meta-proc A process soup is a set ` P` equipped with a partially defined associative composition ` ` (a partial semigroup), with identities where relevant.

paper_title: Six Birds: — Foundations of Emergence Calculus
name: Interface lens (D-META-LENS-01)

paper_title: Six Birds: — Foundations of Emergence Calculus
name: Self-generated primitives
label: thm:meta-prim
compact: thm:meta-prim Assume D-META-PROC-01, D-META-LENS-01, D-META-REF-01, and D-META-BND-01. Then the six primitives P1--P6 appear canonically as closure mechanics. Here P5, P6, P4, and P2 are by construction from the lens/refinement data, while P1 and P3 isolate the only nontrivial compatibility requirements as named hypothesis slots (HL-META-1/2/3). • P5 (Packaging). Each equivalence ` _j` yields a quotient/packaging map ` _j: P→ P/ _j` and induces an idempotent saturation on predicates/events via `cl_j(A):= _j^-1( _j(A))` (cf.\ Sections sec:closure and sec:idempotent-endo). • P6 (Accounting). The refinement order on quotients induces a preorder and monotone ``audit'' quantities (e.g.\ `j↦ |X_j|`); this is an information/feasibility order only (not, by itself, a thermodynamic arrow-of-time). • P4 (Staging). The refinement chain generates a depth index `j`, and bounded interfaces ensure `|X_j| (j+1)`. Nontrivial staging corresponds to strict refinement at some scale (HL-META-2: ` _j+1 _j` for some `j`). • P2 (Constraints). Feasible macrostates are those representable as images under ` _j`, yielding a constraint set carved by interface compatibility. • P1 (Operator rewrite). Fix a micro-update `F: P→ P`. The induced macro-update `F^ ([p]) := [F(p)]` on ` P/ _j` is well-defined iff `p _j q F(p) _j F(q)` (HL-META-1). When (HL-META-1) fails, one must either (i) refine the lens so stability holds, (ii) modify/extend `F` to respect ` _j`, or (iii) accept that no closed macro dynamics exists at depth `j`. • P3 (Holonomy). Assuming there exist two admissible closure/evolution routes with the same input/output type (HL-META-3) (e.g.\ ` _j F` versus `F^ _j` when `F^ ` is well-defined), their discrepancy defines a holonomy-like diagnostic. In normed operator instantiations we measure this by `RM(j)` (Appendix app:tk-defects, Eq. eq:tk-rm); this is a discrepancy diagnostic, not itself a directionality certificate (see Section sec:aot).

paper_title: Six Birds: — Foundations of Emergence Calculus

paper_title: Six Birds: — Foundations of Emergence Calculus

paper_title: Six Birds: — Foundations of Emergence Calculus

Canonical instantiations in this manuscript include: • the information/feasibility order induced by limited access (META), • path-space KL asymmetry with data processing — (Section sec:aot), • the ACC graph 1-form/cycle-integral audit — (Section sec:acc).

label: rem:tk-bridge-to-primitives

paper_title: Six Birds: — Foundations of Emergence Calculus
name: Non-implication: why ECT is an add-on, not automatic
label: rem:ect-nonimplication
compact: rem:ect-nonimplication The ECT conclusion is not a consequence of passivity alone. Passivity (existence of a storage functional with `S(t)-S(s) ∈t_s^t u, Z u `) does not by itself control ICAP constants, does not force mode compression, and does not eliminate lossless feasible directions. Even within convolution/finite-memory classes, passivity alone allows arbitrarily large ICAP constants via high-Q slowly decaying internal directions; the balanced coupling condition (Definition def:ect-bal) is one explicit way to exclude this. The template therefore isolates explicit structural sources of coercivity/capacity control: P4-style sector compression (bounded sector complexity), P5 packaging outcomes (e.g.\ atomization with finite memory), and P2 feasibility that removes null directions. These conditions couple packaging+accounting to a throughput certificate, but they do not by themselves imply novelty (Section sec:forcing) or directionality (Sections sec:acc--sec:aot).

name: Six primitives (P1--P6), in framework language
label: rem:six-primitives
compact: rem:six-primitives Fix a space ` P` of protocol objects (discrete descriptions) equipped with a refinement chain, modeled as a family of equivalences ` _j` indexed by a stage parameter `j` (or, in analysis notation, by a step size `h 0`). Write ` _j: P→ P/ _j` for the quotient/packaging map. Then the six primitives may be read as follows: • \ (Packaging). Each equivalence ` _j` yields a quotient/packaging map ` _j` and induces an idempotent saturation on predicates/events via \[ cl_j(A) := _j^-1( _j(A)). \] This is a standard closure-operator construction in order/lattice settings; see e.g.\ . In analytic instantiations, ` _j` is a limit/identification map (``equal up to `o(1)` as `h→ 0`''); in algebraic instantiations it is a literal quotient by a congruence. • \ (Accounting). The refinement order on quotients induces a preorder and monotone defect/audit quantities (e.g.\ `j↦ Def(j)` or `h↦ Err(h)`). In this mathematics instantiation, ``accounting'' is a feasibility ledger (error control), not a directionality certificate. • \ (Staging). The refinement chain generates the stage index `j` (or `h`). Nontrivial staging corresponds to strict refinement at some scale (a genuine increase in resolution rather than a reparameterization). • \ (Constraints). Feasible macrostates at depth `j` are those representable as images under ` _j`. Concretely, this is where invariances (translation/rotation/scale), locality, linearity, and algebra-compatibility are imposed as coherence conditions on the packaged layer. • \ (Operator rewrite). Fix a micro-update or micro-operator `F: P→ P`. The induced macro-update `F^ ([p]) := [F(p)]` on ` P/ _j` is well-defined iff \[ p _j q \ \ F(p) _j F(q). \] When this fails, one must either refine the lens (change ` _j`), modify/extend `F` (renormalize / rescale / rewrite it), or accept that no closed macro dynamics exists at depth `j`. • \ (Protocol / holonomy). When there exist two admissible closure/evolution routes with the same input/output type (e.g.\ ``refine then apply'' versus ``apply then refine''), their discrepancy defines a holonomy-like diagnostic. In normed instantiations we measure this by a route-mismatch quantity `RM`: a number that should decay under refinement in stable regimes.

name: Mathematics theory package
label: def:math-theory-package
compact: def:math-theory-package A mathematics theory package is a tuple \[ T = (Z,\ f,\ _f,\ E,\ D) \] where: • `Z` is a carrier of discrete protocol objects at a chosen stage (e.g.\ grid functions, truncated sums/products, finite compositions, Cauchy sequences of rationals). • `f:Z→ X` is a lens (a coarse description map). The induced definability structure ` _f` is the family of predicates on `Z` that are visible through `f` (equivalently: constant on fibers of `f`). • `E: V→ V` is a completion/packaging endomap on a chosen description space ` V` associated to `Z` (often idempotent or approximately idempotent in a specified norm). The fixed points of `E` are the internally complete objects recognized by the theory at the chosen scale. • ` D` is a defect ledger: a designated family of nonnegative diagnostics (error bounds, residual norms, route mismatch statistics) together with a monotonicity principle under refinement/coarsening. In this mathematics instantiation, ` D` records feasibility (stability under refinement), not a thermodynamic arrow-of-time.

name: Slogan
label: rem:math-is-theory
compact: rem:math-is-theory The title phrase ``A mathematics is A theory'' is used in the following technical sense: to introduce a stable mathematical layer is to specify (i) what discrete protocol objects are being staged, (ii) what identifications are permitted under refinement, (iii) what completion/packaging map is being used, and (iv) what defect ledger certifies that the packaged layer is coherent.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: Six Birds primitives and the present paper
label: rem:six-birds-primitives
compact: rem:six-birds-primitives We use the Six Birds vocabulary of closure mechanics introduced in . The six primitives are: • P1: operator rewrite, • P2: constraints or feasibility gating, • P3: route mismatch / holonomy, • P4: staging, • P5: packaging, • P6: accounting / audit. The present paper is primarily a P3 paper. Its central object is local route mismatch in rewriting systems. P5 and P6 play supporting roles by packaging the rewriting layers and by keeping the defect structure explicit in machine-readable artifacts and audits. The mathematical development below is otherwise self-contained.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: Bare graph surrogates are not diagnostic for confluence
label: prop:bare-graph-not-diagnostic
compact: prop:bare-graph-not-diagnostic The graph-only surrogates above do not diagnose confluence, even in the small terminating finite-ARS regime explored in this paper.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: From graph loops to branching cells
label: rem:graph-loops-to-branching-cells
compact: rem:graph-loops-to-branching-cells The negative result of this section is therefore a positive design constraint for the rest of the paper. Any viable confluence-as-flatness statement must be formulated on a structure that remembers local branching cells. In the present paper, that structure is the reduction 2-complex. The local obstructions of interest are then carried by generating `2`-cells, not by graph loops in the bare reduction graph.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: Reduction 2-complex
label: def:reduction-two-complex
compact: def:reduction-two-complex For the purposes of this paper, a reduction 2-complex associated to a rewriting system `R` consists of the following data. • A set of `0`-cells, namely the states, words, or terms under consideration. • A set of directed `1`-cells, namely the one-step rewrites `x → y`. • A set of generating `2`-cells, each attached to a local two-route branching pattern with common source. In the finite-ARS setting these are local peaks. In the string and term-rewriting settings used in this paper, these are reachable critical pairs relative to the chosen start states and exploration bounds.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: Why the bare graph is insufficient
label: rem:bare-graph-insufficient
compact: rem:bare-graph-insufficient A graph by itself can encode paths, but not which pairs of paths are the elementary local branchings whose agreement is at stake. Curvature language therefore cannot be attached to the bare reduction graph alone in any informative way. The relevant local obstruction lives on generating `2`-cells, not merely on loops in the `1`-skeleton. This is exactly why the graph-only flatness surrogates examined in sec:bare-graph-not-enough fail.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: Boundary data and fillers
label: def:boundary-filler-data
compact: def:boundary-filler-data Let ` ` be a generating `2`-cell with source `x` and one-step branches to `y_ ` and `y_r`. Its boundary data consist of \[ x → y_ and x → y_r. \] A filler for ` ` is a common descendant `w` together with directed paths \[ y_ →^* w and y_r →^* w. \] When such a filler exists, we call `w` a join witness for ` `.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: Elementary holonomy status
label: def:elementary-holonomy-status
compact: def:elementary-holonomy-status Let ` ` be a generating `2`-cell in a reduction 2-complex. • ` ` has trivial elementary holonomy if it admits a filler in the sense of def:boundary-filler-data. • ` ` has nontrivial elementary holonomy if no such filler exists.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: Elementary holonomy and the theorem-level core
label: rem:holonomy-vs-formal-core
compact: rem:holonomy-vs-formal-core The theorem-level core proved in sec:core-theorem uses only joinability of elementary peaks. The normal-form mismatch diagnostic belongs to the computational layer for terminating explored examples and is useful precisely because it refines the nontrivial cases. It is not needed for the basic equivalence between elementary flatness and local confluence.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: Joinability
label: def:joinability
compact: def:joinability Two states `b,c ∈ X` are joinable if there exists some `d ∈ X` such that \[ b →^* d and c →^* d. \]

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: Normal forms
label: def:normal-form
compact: def:normal-form A state `n ∈ X` is a normal form if there is no state `m ∈ X` such that `n → m`.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: Local confluence
label: def:local-confluence
compact: def:local-confluence The rewriting system `(X,→)` is locally confluent if for all `a,b,c ∈ X`, \[ a → b and a → c b and c are joinable. \]

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: Elementary peaks and elementary flatness
label: def:elementary-peak-flatness
compact: def:elementary-peak-flatness An elementary peak is a triple `(a,b,c)` such that \[ a → b, a → c, b ≠ c. \] The rewriting system `(X,→)` is elementarily flat if every elementary peak is joinable.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: Reflexive joinability
label: lem:joinable-refl
compact: lem:joinable-refl Every state is joinable with itself.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: Elementary flatness iff local confluence
label: thm:elementary-flatness-iff-local-confluence
compact: thm:elementary-flatness-iff-local-confluence A rewriting system is elementarily flat if and only if it is locally confluent.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: What the theorem does and does not say
label: rem:core-theorem-scope
compact: rem:core-theorem-scope thm:elementary-flatness-iff-local-confluence is the formal core of the paper. It does not yet identify which local branchings generate the relevant `2`-cells in a given rewriting formalism; that is the role of critical pairs in sec:critical-pairs-curvature. Nor does it by itself supply a local-to-global theorem such as Newman-style termination plus local confluence . Its point is narrower and more precise: once the correct elementary branchings have been identified, ``flatness'' at that level is exactly local confluence.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: Confluence and normalization
label: def:confluence-normalization
compact: def:confluence-normalization The rewriting system `(X,→)` is confluent if for all `a,b,c ∈ X`, \[ a →^* b and a →^* c b and c are joinable. \] It is normalizing if for every `a ∈ X` there exists some normal form `n` such that \[ a →^* n. \]

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: Confluence and normalization give a unique normal form
label: prop:confluence-normalization-unique-normal-form
compact: prop:confluence-normalization-unique-normal-form Assume that `(X,→)` is confluent and normalizing. Then for every `a ∈ X` there exists a unique normal form `n` such that `a →^* n`.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: Lean formal core
label: rem:lean-formal-core-crossref
compact: rem:lean-formal-core-crossref The definitions and baseline equivalences used in this section are mirrored in the Lean development summarized in Appendix app:lean-formal-core. In particular, the formal core contains the elementary-flatness/local-confluence equivalence together with the corresponding uniqueness-of-normal-form statement under confluence and normalization.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: Reachable critical pairs capture the observed local obstruction set in the curated string examples
label: prop:reachable-critical-pairs-capture-string-obstructions
compact: prop:reachable-critical-pairs-capture-string-obstructions For the curated string examples `E005`--`E008`, the reachable critical pairs match the graph-extracted local peaks, and their defect signatures agree.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: The curated left-linear term-rewriting bridge exhibits the same local generator pattern
label: prop:trs-critical-pairs-as-curvature-generators
compact: prop:trs-critical-pairs-as-curvature-generators In the curated left-linear term-rewriting examples `TRS002`--`TRS004`, reachable critical pairs agree with graph-visible local peaks, and their defect status agrees with the local confluence behavior observed in the explored reduction graphs.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: Why the qualifier reachable matters
label: rem:reachable-critical-pairs-matter
compact: rem:reachable-critical-pairs-matter The phrase critical pairs are curvature generators would be too coarse if interpreted as a statement about every system critical pair independently of context. The correct local layer for the explored reduction complex is the reachable critical-pair layer relative to chosen starts. This is not a technicality. It is exactly what separates the system-wide overlap inventory from the local generator set that actually appears in the reduction 2-complex under study.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: Exhaustive finite-ARS stress test
label: prop:exhaustive-finite-ars-stress-test
compact: prop:exhaustive-finite-ars-stress-test Within the terminating finite-ARS search space on up to four states, the four target discrepancy classes tracked in the repository are empty.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: What the computational bridge does and does not establish
label: rem:computational-bridge-scope
compact: rem:computational-bridge-scope The computational evidence in this section is strong enough to fix the correct local geometric picture. It is not, by itself, the final theorem package for finite terminating left-linear term rewriting systems in full generality. What it does establish is that the corrected local/global story survives every implemented stress test: exhaustive finite ARS search in the terminating regime, curated string overlaps and completion pairs, and curated left-linear term-rewriting examples with genuine nonroot overlap.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: Completion as holonomy elimination in the explicit before/after pairs
label: prop:completion-as-holonomy-elimination
compact: prop:completion-as-holonomy-elimination In the explicit string pair `E007`--`E008` and the explicit term-rewriting pair `TRS003`--`TRS004`, the added rule leaves the local generator intact while eliminating its defect. In both cases: • the relevant local branching source persists; • the generating `2`-cell changes from nontrivial elementary holonomy to trivial elementary holonomy; • the local defect counts drop to zero; • the explored system changes from nonconfluent to confluent.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: Boundary of the claim
label: rem:completion-boundary
compact: rem:completion-boundary Nothing in this section is meant to identify completion in full generality with a geometric algorithm on reduction complexes. The claim is narrower. In the explicit case studies implemented here, the added rule removes a local route mismatch carried by a generating `2`-cell, and that removal coincides with restoration of confluence in the explored system. This is enough to justify the operational reading of completion as holonomy elimination, and no stronger algorithmic statement is needed for the paper.

paper_title: To Flatten a Stone with Six Birds: — [4pt] Critical Pairs, Holonomy, and Confluence — in Rewriting Systems
name: The remaining gap is not more code
label: rem:remaining-gap-not-code
compact: rem:remaining-gap-not-code At this point, the repository has already done the experimental work needed for this paper. The finite-ARS audits are frozen, the string and term-rewriting bridges are frozen, the reduction 2-complex layer is explicit, the completion case studies are explicit, and the claim-support matrix records the current evidence boundary. What remains is theorem writing, literature positioning, and final manuscript discipline rather than new implementation.

paper_title: To Lay a Stone with Six Birds: Finite-State Semantics for Packaging, Directionality, and Coarse-Graining
name: Substrate (informal)
label: def:substrate
compact: def:substrate A substrate ` S` consists of: (i) a state carrier `Z` (finite in our canonical machine model), (ii) a composable dynamics primitive (autonomous in the canonical model), and (iii) an admissible family of deterministic observational maps (lenses) from `Z` to coarser description spaces. Additional internal structure may be present (e.g.\ registers, ledgers, prototype selectors), but must be represented as part of state or as derived operators.

paper_title: To Lay a Stone with Six Birds: Finite-State Semantics for Packaging, Directionality, and Coarse-Graining
name: Realization (informal)
label: def:realization
compact: def:realization A realization of a primitive on ` S` is a specification of internal operators and constraints on ` S` that instantiate the primitive without introducing external oracles. Concretely, realizations may be given by endomaps on distributions or predicates, deterministically induced coarse-grainings, internal audit functionals, and internal composition rules.

paper_title: To Lay a Stone with Six Birds: Finite-State Semantics for Packaging, Directionality, and Coarse-Graining
name: No smuggling
label: def:no-smuggling
compact: def:no-smuggling A construction smuggles a primitive if it requires information or structure not representable within the substrate state and its admitted operators. Equivalently, a primitive is realized without smuggling if it is definable using only: (i) the substrate state carrier, (ii) the admitted compositional dynamics, (iii) deterministic lenses and their induced constructions, and (iv) internal endomaps/audits constructed from the above. External schedules, externally declared equivalence relations, and externally imposed audits that are not induced by the substrate are disallowed.

paper_title: To Lay a Stone with Six Birds: Finite-State Semantics for Packaging, Directionality, and Coarse-Graining
name: Operational reading
compact: A convenient way to read def:no-smuggling is syntactic: treat a substrate as presenting a signature of admissible constructors (state, dynamics, lenses, induced linear maps, endomaps, and audits), and treat ``without smuggling'' as definability in the term algebra generated by that signature. We do not develop a full syntactic metatheory here; the witness suite and the theorems in sec:theorems use only this disciplined notion of ``no external oracles.''

paper_title: To Lay a Stone with Six Birds: Finite-State Semantics for Packaging, Directionality, and Coarse-Graining
name: Lens
label: def:lens
compact: def:lens A lens is a deterministic map `f:Z→ X`. We interpret `f` as the observational interface: two microstates `z,z'∈ Z` are observationally indistinguishable at scale `f` if `f(z)=f(z')`.

paper_title: To Lay a Stone with Six Birds: Finite-State Semantics for Packaging, Directionality, and Coarse-Graining
name: Definability from a lens
label: def:definability
compact: def:definability A predicate `h:Z→\0,1\` is definable from a lens `f:Z→ X` if `h` is constant on fibers of `f`, i.e.\ if `f(z)=f(z')` implies `h(z)=h(z')`. Equivalently, there exists ` h:X→\0,1\` such that `h= h f`.

paper_title: To Lay a Stone with Six Birds: Finite-State Semantics for Packaging, Directionality, and Coarse-Graining
name: Refinement
label: def:refinement
compact: def:refinement A lens `f_2:Z→ X_2` refines `f_1:Z→ X_1` if there exists a deterministic map `g:X_2→ X_1` such that `f_1=g f_2`. We write `f_2 f_1`.

paper_title: To Lay a Stone with Six Birds: Finite-State Semantics for Packaging, Directionality, and Coarse-Graining
name: Packaging endomap
label: def:packaging-endomap
compact: def:packaging-endomap A packaging endomap is a function `e: → ` (for an appropriate carrier ` `) that is exactly or approximately idempotent. Exact idempotence is the equation `e e = e`. When ` ` is a set of descriptions, `Fix(e)=\x∈ : e(x)=x\` are the packaged objects.

paper_title: To Lay a Stone with Six Birds: Finite-State Semantics for Packaging, Directionality, and Coarse-Graining
name: Packaging equivalence
label: def:packeq
compact: def:packeq Given `e: → `, define a relation ` _e` on ` ` by \[ x _e y e(x)=e(y). \] We call ` _e` the packaging equivalence induced by `e`.

paper_title: To Lay a Stone with Six Birds: Finite-State Semantics for Packaging, Directionality, and Coarse-Graining

paper_title: To Lay a Stone with Six Birds: Finite-State Semantics for Packaging, Directionality, and Coarse-Graining
name: Compilation to ` S_ ` up to packaging equivalence
label: thm:normal-form
compact: thm:normal-form Let ` S` be a substrate that realizes P1--P6 without smuggling in the sense of def:no-smuggling. Assume further that the realized operators are finitary (state and registers can be encoded in a finite carrier) and autonomous once all protocol state is represented. Then there exists a substrate ` M∈ S_ ` and an encoding of ` S` into ` M` such that: [leftmargin=*, itemsep=0.25em] • the lens/refinement structure of ` S` is simulated by deterministic lenses on ` M`, • packaging in ` S` is simulated by internal packaging endomaps on ` M` up to packaging equivalence, and • admissible audits in ` S` are represented by intrinsic audits on ` M` (in particular, directionality audits respect monotonicity under coarse-graining). Moreover, if two compilations choose the same canonical prototype-selection scheme for each lens (e.g.\ uniform-on-fiber) and the same auditing conventions, then they are mutually simulable up to packaging equivalence via packaging-respecting maps in the sense of def:pack-morphism.

paper_title: To Lay a Stone with Six Birds: Finite-State Semantics for Packaging, Directionality, and Coarse-Graining
name: No-smuggling separations
label: thm:minimality
compact: thm:minimality The following substrate features are necessary (up to equivalent internal encodings) to realize the corresponding primitives without smuggling: [leftmargin=*, itemsep=0.35em] • Autonomy requires phase-in-state (P3). If a substrate permits staged protocols but does not represent protocol state internally, then stroboscopic composition can produce apparent arrows of time that vanish once the dynamics is made autonomous by lifting state. Therefore, any autonomous semantics for protocols must encode phase-in-state (or an equivalent internal mechanism). • Genuine arrows require internal drive (P6drive). Autonomy plus staging does not imply directionality. In an autonomous lifted model with reversible internal phase dynamics, protocol-induced arrows can disappear (` _T 0`). To obtain a genuine arrow in an autonomous substrate, one needs internal drive detectable by a nonzero affinity class (ACC cycle integrals). • Audits must be monotone under coarse-graining (P6). There exist processes with real micro irreversibility but macro observations whose path law is reversal-invariant (` _T^macro=0`). Any audit that reports increased directionality after coarse-graining violates limited-access semantics and is therefore smuggled. • Packaging must be an internal (approximate) idempotent endomap (P5). Without an internal endomap `e` (or closure operator) that induces packaging equivalence `x _e yiff e(x)=e(y)`, there is no internal notion of ``same packaged object'' and no internal fixed-point criterion for stability. Declaring macrostates by fiat is smuggling. • Route mismatch is distinct from directionality (P3 vs.\ P6). Packaging along different refinement routes can yield a measurable holonomy defect (route mismatch), even when directionality audits obey data processing. Therefore, route mismatch must be treated as its own certificate family and cannot be conflated with an arrow audit.

paper_title: To Lay a Stone with Six Birds: Finite-State Semantics for Packaging, Directionality, and Coarse-Graining
name: Status and scope
compact: The theorems above isolate the semantic content needed to turn SPT into a machine semantics. They are stated at a level that cleanly separates: (i) algebraic infrastructure (idempotents/closure), (ii) audit infrastructure (monotone directionality/drive certificates), and (iii) autonomy discipline (phase-in-state for protocols). label: rem:saturation
compact: rem:saturation Corollary cor:packagechange is one instance of a general anti-laddering discipline: a fixed completion under a bounded generation budget cannot produce unbounded object growth by self-iteration. Read against incompleteness, the resonance is deliberate. G\"odel's theorems say a fixed, sufficiently expressive deductive apparatus does not exhaust arithmetic truth and cannot, by iterating its own moves, reach its own consistency. Theorem thm:nonattain says a fixed finite packaging apparatus does not reach the infinite and cannot, by iterating, get there; ` ` lies outside and must be adjoined. Same shape: a closed apparatus, run to saturation, with the novelty placed deliberately out of reach. The other half of the shape---what adjoining actually does---is the subject of :forcing. We flag this as structural framing, not a metatheorem (); each half is a theorem, the kinship between them is a reading.

paper_title: To Set a Stone with Six Birds: — The Free and Purchased Parts of ZFC
name: Why this matters, and a guard
label: rem:translation
compact: rem:translation Theorem thm:translation licenses the one-sorted bookkeeping of the rest of the paper: when we speak of the membership shadow ``satisfying `ZF`,'' no staging content has been silently dropped. It also explains why `ZFC` can afford to be flat: the staging is not external scaffolding but internally recoverable data---the one-sorted derivation of the axioms from the stage picture is the classical complement of this recovery . The infinitary analogue, the definability of the von Neumann rank in `ZF`, is standard . The losslessness is special to the canonical, rank labeling and is not a claim about arbitrary stage maps. A uniform first-order recovery exists for rank; it cannot exist for every labeling, by cardinality---there are only countably many formulas (even with finitely many parameters), but uncountably many maps ` → _fin`. So some staging would be genuinely lost under erasure; the point is that the set-theoretic staging is exactly the one that is not.

Every surjection `f: Z→ X` between finite sets admits a section, constructed without any choice principle (the least-index preimage); a section of `f` is the same datum as a prototype family for the lens. Over `ZF`, the following are equivalent: (1) the Axiom of Choice; (2) every surjection of sets admits a section; (3) every fibered lens admits a canonical-lift prototype family; (4) every product of nonempty sets is nonempty.

label: thm:ch

(a) If `ZF` is consistent, so is `ZFC+CH` (the constructible inner-model packaging, Godel1938,Godel1940). (b) If `ZF` is consistent, so is `ZFC+ ` (a generic-extension packaging adjoining ` _2` Cohen reals, Cohen1963; the ccc cardinal-preservation analysis is part of the imported machinery, Kunen2011). Read through Table tab:correspondence: one substrate admits two lawful completions---an inner-model packaging and a generic-extension packaging---with `CH` true in the first and false in the second. paper_title: To Set a Stone with Six Birds: — The Free and Purchased Parts of ZFC
name: The set layer is not a unique package
label: rem:notunique
compact: rem:notunique Theorem thm:ch is the positive form of one of our non-claims. We do not claim `ZFC` is the unique or canonical promoted set layer; the continuum hypothesis is precisely a place where two completions of the same substrate disagree, and Cohen's mechanism ( :strict) supplies the disagreement on the generic side. The pluralist reading of such disagreements as distinct, equally legitimate universes is the set-theoretic multiverse of ; the opposing universe view (e.g.\ Godel1947) holds that one of them is correct. We construct no model, reprove no independence result, and adjudicate nothing between the completions: which packaging, if any, is ``correct'' is not a question this paper takes a position on. Independence is, on this reading, the expected signature of a foundation that grows by lawful extension---the footprint, at the scale of set theory, of the extension law.

name: Logic layer
label: def:logic-layer
compact: def:logic-layer Fix a microstate space \(Z\), a lens \(f : Z → X\), and an evaluation window \( \). A logic layer at \((f, )\) consists of a nontrivial family \(B ⊆ _f\) of binary packaged predicates together with induced macro-updates such that: • Stability. Each \(b ∈ B\) is metastable on the timescale \( \). • Closure. The relevant micro-updates descend to macro-operators on the packaged variables with small closure defect. • Feasibility semantics. Each \(b ∈ B\) is the indicator of a stable feasible set, and the connective operations required at the layer remain definable there. • Auditability. Persistence, route agreement, and information loss are measurable by explicit diagnostics. When these conditions fail, a symbolic description may still be convenient, but it does not constitute a closed logic layer in the sense used in this paper.

paper_title: The Usefulness of Non-Descending Objects: A Six Birds Theory of Mathematical Applicability
name: SAU synthesis: usefulness through recurring audited profiles
label: thm:sau-final-synthesis
compact: thm:sau-final-synthesis Within the scope of the theorem stack developed in this paper, the usefulness of mathematics is explained by the recurrence of strict audited descent profiles across theory layers. More precisely, whenever a lower problem family \( P\) is SAU-covered by a finite profile registry \( R\), the usefulness claims for the family are licensed by: \[ lower-layer saturation, strict promotion, non-descending promoted structure, audited descending output, no-overreading. \] The resulting explanation is profile-level rather than object-level: mathematical structures become portable because their descent profiles can recur across distinct substrates.
